Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106870; File No. SR-24X-2026-30]
November 10, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 3, 2026, 24X National Exchange LLC (“24X” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to (1) amend 24X Rule 14.1(a) to add express cross-references to 24X Rules 3.7 and 3.21; (2) delete 24X Rule 14.1(b)(1) in its entirety, thereby removing the requirement that the Exchange distribute an information circular to Members
[
3
]
prior to the commencement of trading in each UTP Exchange Traded Product
[
4
]
that generally includes the same information as contained in the information circular approved by the listing exchange; (3) amend 24X Rule 14.1(b)(2)(B) to require that the written description referenced therein be provided in a form approved by the listing exchange or prepared by the open-ended management company issuing such securities; and (4) renumber 24X Rules 14.1(b)(2) through (5) as 24X Rules 14.1(b)(1) through (4), respectively. The Exchange has designated this proposal as non-controversial pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
5
]
and provided the Commission with the notice required by Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii) thereunder.
[
6
]
The proposal is similar to a proposal that Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe BZX”) filed with the Commission.
[
7
]
The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://equities.24exchange.com/​regulation
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to eliminate the requirement that the Exchange distribute an information circular to Members prior to the commencement of trading in each UTP Exchange Traded Product that generally includes the same information as contained in the information circular provided by the listing exchange as provided in 24X Rule 14.1(b)(1). The Exchange also proposes to amend 24X Rule 14.1(a) to add express cross-references to 24X Rules 3.7 and 3.21. The Exchange also proposes to amend 24X Rule 14.1(b)(2)(B) to require that the written description referenced therein be provided in a form approved by the listing exchange or prepared by the open-ended management company issuing such securities.
[
8
]
Finally, the Exchange proposes to renumber 24X Rules 14.1(b)(2) through (5) as 24X Rules 14.1(b)(1) through (4), respectively.
24X Rule 14.1(b) governs the trading of UTP Exchange Traded Products, which are securities listed on another national securities exchange that trade on the Exchange pursuant to unlisted trading privileges (“UTP”). Under current 24X Rule 14.1(b)(1), the Exchange must distribute an information circular prior to the commencement of trading in each UTP Exchange Traded Product that generally mirrors the information circular issued by the primary listing exchange, including: (a) the special risks of trading the new Exchange Traded Product; (b) the Exchange Rules that will apply to the new Exchange Traded Product; and (c) information about the dissemination of the value of the underlying assets or indices. The Exchange proposes to delete 24X Rule 14.1(b)(1) in its entirety.
The information circular requirement is unnecessary because the primary listing exchange's information circular already provides Members with the same disclosures the Exchange would otherwise be required to produce. Members have access to the primary listing exchange's information circular prior to the commencement of UTP trading and may rely upon it for the
(
printed page 73328)
same purposes.
[
9
]
The Exchange's issuance of a separate, duplicative circular therefore serves no independent investor protection function.
The Exchange also proposes to amend 24X Rule 14.1(a) to add express cross-references to 24X Rule 3.7 (Recommendations to Customers) and 24X Rule 3.21 (Customer Disclosures). The Exchange is adding express cross-references to those rules in the introductory paragraph of 24X Rule 14.1(a) to enhance their visibility in the context of UTP Exchange Traded Products. These rules already apply to Members by operation of the Exchange's rulebook. The cross-references are intended to make the applicable framework explicit in the context of UTP Exchange Traded Products. 24X Rule 3.7 independently requires Members to ensure that any recommendation of a UTP Exchange Traded Product is suitable for the customer based on the customer's investment profile, a standing obligation that applies regardless of whether the Exchange has issued a product-specific information circular. Similarly, 24X Rule 3.21 independently requires Members to provide customers with a written disclosure of the risks of trading outside of Regular Trading Hours before accepting any order for execution during such sessions, a standing obligation not contingent on the Exchange's issuance of a product-specific information circular.
Because 24X Rule 14.1(b)(1) has historically served as the mechanism through which the Exchange satisfies the notification obligation under 24X Rule 14.1(b)(2)(B), deletion of 24X Rule 14.1(b)(1) necessitates a conforming amendment to 24X Rule 14.1(b)(2)(B). The Exchange proposes to amend 24X Rule 14.1(b)(2)(B) to require that the written description referenced therein be provided in a form approved by the listing exchange or prepared by the open-ended management company issuing such securities. The Exchange will notify Members by information circular that such written description will only be required when mandated by the listing exchange. This amendment is consistent with the broader purpose of the proposed rule change: where the listing exchange's information circular already provides Members with the information necessary to assess a UTP Exchange Traded Product, a duplicative written description obligation serves no independent investor protection function. Members may rely on the listing exchange's information circular in the same manner and to the same effect.
Finally, the Exchange proposes to renumber existing 24X Rules 14.1(b)(2) through (5) as 24X Rules 14.1(b)(1) through (4), respectively.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
10
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
11
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
12
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes the proposed deletion of 24X Rule 14.1(b)(1) is consistent with the Act because the primary listing exchange's information circular already provides. Members with the same disclosures that the Exchange's information circular would contain. The investor protection functions historically served by the information circular requirement are independently addressed through the primary listing exchange's information circular and the Member-level obligations imposed by 24X Rules 3.7 and 3.21, to which the Exchange proposes to add express cross-references in 24X Rule 14.1(a). The proposed amendment to 24X Rule 14.1(b)(2)(B) ensures that where a written description is required, it is provided in a form approved by the listing exchange or prepared by the open-ended management company issuing such securities, thereby aligning the Exchange's requirements with those of the primary listing market. The Exchange will further notify Members by information circular that such written description will only be required when mandated by the listing exchange, ensuring that no duplicative obligation is imposed where the listing exchange has not determined one to be warranted. The renumbering of 24X Rules 14.1(b)(2) through (5) as 24X Rules 14.1(b)(1) through (4) is ministerial. Additionally, as discussed above, the proposal does not raise any novel issues not previously considered by the Commission.
[
13
]
For these reasons, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change eliminates duplicative procedural obligations applicable to the Exchange in its capacity as a UTP trading venue. It does not alter the terms or conditions under which UTP Exchange Traded Products may be traded on the Exchange, impose any new requirements on Members, or affect the ability of any market participant to access the Exchange's markets. Members will continue to have access to the primary listing exchange's information circular prior to the commencement of UTP trading and may rely upon it for the same purposes as the Exchange's information circular. The proposed amendment to 24X Rule 14.1(b)(2)(B) aligns the written description obligation with the primary listing market's requirements and does not impose any burden on Members beyond what the primary listing market itself requires.
[
14
]
Accordingly, the Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change imposes any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section
(
printed page 73329)
19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
15
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
16
]
thereunder. Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; or (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
17
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
18
]
thereunder.
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
19
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b4(f)(6)(iii),
[
20
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay so that the proposed rule change may become operative immediately upon filing. The Exchange states that the proposed rule change eliminates duplicative procedural obligations applicable to the Exchange in its capacity as a UTP trading venue because the primary listing exchange's information circular already provides Members with the same disclosures the Exchange would otherwise be required to produce.
[
21
]
The Exchange also notes that the proposed rule change does not alter the terms or conditions under which UTP Exchange Traded Products may be traded on the Exchange. For these reasons, the Commission finds that waiver of the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Therefore, the Commission hereby waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change to be operative upon filing.
[
22
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-24X-2026-30 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-24X-2026-30. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.  All submissions should refer to file number SR-24X-2026-30 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
23
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106868; File No. SR-FINRA-2026-024]
November 10, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 2, 2026, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (“FINRA”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by FINRA. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
FINRA is proposing to (1) amend the By-Laws of the Corporation (“FINRA By-Laws”), the By-Laws of FINRA Regulation, Inc. (“FINRA Regulation By-Laws”) and the Plan of Allocation and Delegation of Functions by FINRA to Subsidiaries (“Delegation Plan”) to revise FINRA's governance structure, including the composition and operation of the Board of Governors of
(
printed page 73299)
FINRA (“FINRA Board” or “Board”) and committees established by the Board comprising solely Governors (“Board committees”); and (2) amend FINRA's Restated Certificate of Incorporation (“Certificate of Incorporation”) to conform relevant provisions to the amended and restated FINRA By-Laws. The proposed rule change also would make technical and conforming changes to the FINRA By-Laws, FINRA Regulation By-Laws, Delegation Plan, Certificate of Incorporation and FINRA rules.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on FINRA's website at
http://www.finra.org
and at the principal office of FINRA.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, FINRA included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. FINRA has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
Background
The FINRA By-Laws, read together with the Certificate of Incorporation, govern the composition and operation of the FINRA Board. The Board includes individuals from member firms of various sizes and business models, as well as public leaders with expertise in markets, technology, regulatory oversight, business and law. In 1996, FINRA's predecessor, the National Association of Securities Dealers (“NASD”), amended its By-Laws to require that the number of non-industry Governors exceed the number of industry Governors.
[
3
]
The majority public structure was implemented when the By-Laws were last amended in 2007 in connection with the merger of NASD and NYSE Regulation to create FINRA.
[
4
]
The FINRA By-Laws currently provide for a Board composed of up to 25 Governors, with 10 seats designated for “Industry Governors,”
[
5
]
11 to 14 seats designated for “Public Governors”
[
6
]
and one seat reserved for FINRA's Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”), who is considered neither an Industry Governor nor a Public Governor.
Seven of the Industry Governor seats—three Small Firm Governors, one Mid-Size Firm Governor and three Large Firm Governors—are designated for individuals associated with FINRA members that correspond to each firm size. Pursuant to the FINRA By-Laws, a small firm employs at least one and no more than 150 registered persons; a mid-size firm employs at least 151 and no more than 499 registered persons; and a large firm employs 500 or more registered persons. (
See
FINRA By-Laws Article I.) Industry Governors are elected to these seats by the small, mid-size and large member firms, respectively. The three remaining Industry Governor seats are appointed, segment-specific seats,
i.e.,
a “Floor Member Governor,” an “Independent Dealer/Insurance Affiliate Governor” and an “Investment Company Affiliate Governor,” as those terms are defined in the FINRA By-Laws. (
See
FINRA By-Laws Article I.)
Overview of Proposed Amendments
FINRA is proposing to amend the FINRA By-Laws, FINRA Regulation By-Laws and Delegation Plan relating to the composition and operation of the FINRA Board and Board committees to modernize FINRA's governance structure and strengthen FINRA's self-regulatory model. As described below, FINRA is further proposing to amend the Certificate of Incorporation to conform relevant provisions to the amended and restated FINRA By-Laws and to make other updates and technical changes.
Among other changes, the proposed rule change would transition the FINRA Board from a majority of Public Governors to a majority of Industry Governors, while preserving a substantial role for public representatives on the Board—Public Governors would represent from 41.7 to 47.4 percent of the total number of Industry and Public Governors.
[
7
]
The proposed rule change also would potentially broaden industry representation, including among small firms, on the FINRA Board by converting the three appointed, segment-specific industry seats to three appointed, at-large industry seats. And, consistent with modern governance practices, the proposed rule change would reduce the size of the Board, which currently may have up to 25 members, to no more than 20 members.
With respect to the operation of the FINRA Board and Board committees, the proposed rule change would revise term limits, conform quorum requirements and provide more flexibility for the Board to manage the composition of the Board and its committees based on current needs, subject to minimum Industry and Public Governor representation requirements. The Audit Committee would continue to require a majority of Public Governors and continue to be chaired by a Public Governor, as is the case today.
FINRA believes that the proposed rule change would strengthen member engagement, increase access to industry expertise and better position FINRA to protect and serve investors, markets and member firms in an evolving industry and market environment. FINRA believes that the public benefits of the self-regulatory organization (“SRO”) model include the ability to leverage member knowledge, experience and insight. Appropriate member participation in FINRA's programs is important for capturing the deep, practical expertise that is central to self-regulation and helps FINRA effectively
(
printed page 73300)
carry out its mission of protecting investors and market integrity—including by producing better visibility into emerging threats, risky business practices and unfair tactics. In addition, the proposed rule change would provide the Board greater flexibility to draw on expertise from a broader range of business models to adapt to changes in the industry and ensure appropriate representation from across the membership—enhancing opportunities for a wider spectrum of member firms, including more small firms, to participate in governance. Finally, with a somewhat smaller size and greater flexibility to manage its operations, the Board would be more nimble and better able to benefit from the insights of both Industry and Public Governors.
FINRA notes that several of the factors that supported NASD's adoption of a majority non-industry Board over 30 years ago are significantly different from the environment FINRA faces today. NASD's change to its Board composition was one of many changes made in connection with an SEC enforcement action against NASD, which found that NASD failed to adequately oversee the Nasdaq market and that Nasdaq market makers exercised undue influence over NASD's operations and regulatory affairs.
[
8
]
NASD fully divested Nasdaq in 2006, eliminating the market-driven conflicts of interest that had previously existed between NASD's self-regulatory obligations and the competitive incentives of Nasdaq market makers.
[
9
]
And FINRA has a number of important institutional safeguards in place to ensure that it serves its mission of protecting investors and market integrity. These include, in addition to substantial Public Governor involvement, organizational guardrails, procedural requirements and other checks and balances to provide for robust and fair regulatory and disciplinary functions, and greater transparency into FINRA's regulatory operations, rulemaking and finances to facilitate accountability.
More specifically, FINRA maintains a fully independent internal audit staff, which reviews all aspects of FINRA and its subsidiaries and reports directly to what will continue to be a majority public, Public Governor-chaired Audit Committee.
[
10
]
In addition, FINRA's Office of the Ombuds provides an independent, neutral and confidential source of assistance for individuals who have questions or concerns about the activities of FINRA and its employees. FINRA's ombuds staff also reports directly to the Audit Committee.
[
11
]
This structure ensures that the Audit Committee can investigate issues of concern.
[
12
]
To ensure independence in disciplinary functions, FINRA's Office of Hearing Officers (“OHO”) serves as FINRA's adjudicatory forum for disciplinary and expedited proceedings. OHO is an independent office within FINRA that employs impartial professional Hearing Officers who preside over proceedings commenced by FINRA's Enforcement Department. OHO maintains strict independence from FINRA's regulatory and enforcement programs, and Hearing Officers are not involved in the investigative and examination processes of FINRA. Employment protections exist for Hearing Officers to further ensure their independence, and any termination by FINRA's CEO can be appealed to the Audit Committee.
[
13
]
In addition, FINRA's Office of Disciplinary Affairs (“ODA”), which is independent of Enforcement and not involved in the investigation or litigation of cases, is charged with reviewing proposed settlements and complaints. ODA provides an independent review of the legal and evidentiary sufficiency of charges proposed by the Enforcement staff. ODA also reviews settlements for consistency with FINRA's Sanction Guidelines and applicable precedent.
[
14
]
In furtherance of FINRA's mission to protect investors, FINRA's Investor Education Foundation provides educational programs and supports innovative research to protect investors and help them achieve their financial goals.
[
15
]
FINRA also produces regular reports on its activities and finances, with publicly available reports on its budget and financial performance. All FINRA rule changes are subject to public review and comment, and FINRA disciplinary actions are made public. FINRA also produces regular information about its examination program and broader regulatory operations, including insights into findings from those operations.
[
16
]
FINRA believes that these safeguards, among others, along with comprehensive SEC oversight and evaluation of such oversight by the Government Accountability Office (“GAO”),
[
17
]
provide strong assurance that FINRA will continue to perform its investor protection responsibilities while benefiting from the revised governance structure and strengthened self-regulatory model that the proposed rule change provides.
Proposed Amendments Relating to the FINRA Board
FINRA is proposing to amend the FINRA By-Laws with respect to the composition and operation of the FINRA Board as follows.
First,
the proposed rule change would amend the FINRA By-Laws to require that the Board have a majority of Industry Governors. (
See
FINRA By-Laws Article VII, Section 4(a).) The minimum number of Industry Governors would be the seven existing
(
printed page 73301)
elected Industry Governor seats. The number of Public Governors would be required to be one or two less than the number of Industry Governors, meaning that at least 41.7 percent of Industry and Public Governors would be Public Governors. FINRA's CEO would remain on the Board in a seat that is neither Industry nor Public.
Second,
the proposed rule change would amend the FINRA By-Laws to convert the three appointed Industry Governor seats (as noted above, these are the Floor Member Governor, the Independent Dealer/Insurance Affiliate Governor and the Investment Company Affiliate Governor) to appointed At Large Industry Governor seats. (
See
FINRA By-Laws Article VII, Section 4(a).) An “At Large Industry Governor” would be defined as a “member of the Board to be appointed by the Board; provided however, to be eligible to serve, an At Large Industry Governor must qualify as an Industry Governor.” (
See
FINRA By-Laws Article I.) The number of At Large Industry Governor seats would not exceed three.
[
18
]
The FINRA Board would have flexibility to fill these seats based on the needs of FINRA by drawing from the expertise, experience and business models of the entire membership. In addition, the Board would be able to decide whether to further decrease its overall size by reducing the number of At Large Industry Governor seats. In such instance, the Board also would decrease the number of Public Governor seats to maintain the Industry Governor majority. In all scenarios, the total number of Public Governors on the Board would be one or two less than the total number of Industry Governors on the Board, thereby preserving substantial Public Governor participation in Board governance, as illustrated in greater detail below.
Third,
the proposed rule change would reduce the total number of seats on the Board to a maximum of 20, comprising: (1) seven to 10 Industry Governors (seven elected Industry Governors,
i.e.,
three Small Firm Governors, one Mid-Size Firm Governor and three Large Firm Governors, and zero to three appointed At Large Industry Governors (as determined by the Board)); (2) five to nine Public Governors (as determined by the Board, always one or two less than the total number of Industry Governors); and (3) FINRA's CEO. As amended, Article VII, Section 4(a) of the FINRA By-Laws would provide that the FINRA Board shall consist of no fewer than 13 nor more than 20 Governors.
As noted, the proposed rule change provides for substantial continued public representation on the Board, with Public Governors comprising at least 41.7 percent of the total number of Industry and Public Governors. For example, if the Board has the minimum number of Industry Governors,
i.e.,
the seven elected Industry Governor seats, then the number of Public Governors can be no less than five and no more than six. If there are five Public Governors (
i.e.,
two less than the number of Industry Governors), then the Public Governors would comprise 41.7 percent of the total number of Industry and Public Governors. If there are six Public Governors (
i.e.,
one less than the number of Industry Governors), then the Public Governors would comprise 46.2 percent.
If the Board has the maximum number of Industry Governors,
i.e.,
the seven elected Industry Governor seats and the three appointed At Large Industry Governor seats, then the number of Public Governors can be no less than eight and no more than nine. If there are eight Public Governors (
i.e.,
two less than the number of Industry Governors), then the Public Governors would comprise 44.4 percent of the total number of Industry and Public Governors. If there are nine Public Governors (
i.e.,
one less than the number of Industry Governors), then the Public Governors would comprise 47.4 percent.
[
19
]
Fourth,
the proposed rule change would amend the FINRA By-laws to revise the quorum requirements to reflect the changes to the Board's composition. Specifically, a majority of the Board, including not less than 50 percent of the Public Governor members (which is currently required) and 50 percent of the Industry Governor members (which would be a new requirement) would be needed to constitute a quorum of the Board. (
See
FINRA By-Laws Article VII, Section 8.)
Finally,
the proposed rule change would amend the FINRA By-Laws to extend the current Board term limits from two consecutive three-year terms to three consecutive three-year terms. (
See
FINRA By-Laws Article VII, Section 5.) This would provide the possibility that Governors could serve for up to nine years (versus six years currently).
[
20
]
Section 5 would also be amended to clarify that any appointed or elected Governor who fills a vacancy of a Governor position or a new Governor position shall serve for the remaining term of the class
[
21
]
or until a successor is duly appointed and qualified, or until death, resignation, disqualification or removal.
Proposed Amendments Relating to the FINRA Board Committees
The FINRA By-Laws provide for the following Board committees: the Nominating Committee,
[
22
]
Executive Committee, Audit Committee
[
23
]
and Finance Committee.
[
24
]
(
See
FINRA By-Laws Article VII, Section 9, and Article IX, Sections 4, 5 and 6, respectively.) The FINRA By-Laws also provide generally for any other committee or subcommittee appointed by the Board. (
See
FINRA By-Laws Article IX, Section 1(b).) Additional Board committees are provided for under the FINRA Regulation By-Laws (specifically, the FINRA Regulation Board of Directors (“FINRA Regulation Board”)
[
25
]
under Article IV) and the Delegation Plan (specifically, the Management Compensation Committee (“Compensation Committee”)
[
26
]
under Section I.C.).
[
27
]
FINRA is proposing to modify composition and other requirements for the Board committees and subcommittees as follows.
First,
the proposed rule change would amend the FINRA By-Laws to establish
(
printed page 73302)
minimum composition requirements for Board committees, as set out below. Subject to these requirements, other Board committee governance requirements (
e.g.,
number and composition of committee members and Chair designation) would be established by the Board in the committees' respective governing documents. FINRA believes that the proposed rule change to revise FINRA's Board governance structure provides for the organization of FINRA in a manner that will continue to enable FINRA to carry out the purposes of the Act and to comply and enforce compliance by FINRA members with the Act. FINRA believes that the proposed rule change assures a fair representation of FINRA's members in the selection of its Governors and administration of its affairs and complies with the public participant requirements of the Act, including the issuer and investor representation requirement.
As discussed above, the proposed rule change would transition the FINRA Board to a majority of Industry Governors, while preserving a substantial role for public representatives on the Board. Seven Industry Governor seats (
i.e.,
three Small Firm Governors, one Mid-Size Firm Governor and three Large Firm Governors) would continue to be elected by small, mid-size and large member firms, respectively. The conversion of three appointed segment-specific Industry seats to three appointed At Large Industry seats would potentially broaden industry representation, including among small firms.
FINRA members will continue to have extensive involvement in the administration of FINRA's affairs through participation in advisory committees, disciplinary hearing panels and the National Adjudicatory Council, among others. The Commission has previously found that such participation further provides for the fair representation of members in the administration of the affairs of an SRO, particularly with respect to participation on committees relating to rulemaking and relating to the disciplinary process.

At the same time, the proposed rule change would preserve a substantial role for public representatives on the Board by requiring that the number of Public Governors on the Board be one or two less than the number of Industry Governors. The Public Governors would represent no less than 41.7 percent of the total number of Industry and Public Governors on the Board. In addition, the proposed rule change provides for a minimum number of Public Governors on Board committees, and the Audit Committee must continue to be public majority and chaired by a Public Governor. The Commission has previously found that Public Governors, none of which may have a material relationship with a broker or dealer or registered SRO, satisfy the requirement under the Act to have at least one director representative of issuers and investors.

B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
FINRA does not believe that the proposed rule change will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The regulatory need for the proposed rule change is described above in Item II.A.1.
Economic Baseline
The economic baseline for the proposed rule change consists of the current FINRA By-Laws governing the composition, structure and operation of the FINRA Board and its committees.
In general, corporate boards provide direction, monitoring and accountability to help ensure stewardship and enable the organization to have access to vital external resources and information.
[
53
]
As the Board of an SRO, FINRA's Board differs from conventional corporate boards in that it is meant to provide fair representation across its membership and serve the other statutory requirements of the Act.
[
54
]
Although there may be broad agreement on the importance of these requirements, individual Governors may differ in their perspectives and beliefs as how to best meet FINRA's statutory obligations. Industry Governors will typically have more technical and detailed current knowledge regarding the brokerage industry, member-firm business models and evolving industry conditions, while Public Governors will have a wider variety of backgrounds reflective of the governance needs of the organization, which will not always include knowledge of the brokerage industry that is comparable to Industry Governors.
Industry and Public Governors will, given the requirements of their classification, have different backgrounds, business affiliations and relationships. Each individual Governor will be informed by their own experience and current situation, thus perspectives, knowledge and incentives may differ both between the groups and among Governors within each group. The balance of these may influence the Board's oversight of and advice to management and, in turn, how FINRA fulfills its mission.
[
55
]
Differences among
(
printed page 73308)
Industry Governors' interests and incentives along with substantial participation by Public Governors can contribute to ensuring balance in governance and fulfillment of FINRA's statutory obligations. These same characteristics of the board also support the public's confidence in its stewardship of the public interest.
The relevance of the extent and type of expertise accessible to the Board and Board committees will vary depending on the context. For example, when considering if or how to respond to new industry products or business practices, detailed technical Board knowledge informed by different experiences may be of particular importance. In other contexts, there may be a stronger emphasis on the Board's needs in broader areas that extend outside the industry, such as corporate governance, technology management or public policy.
Economic Impacts
The proposed rule change would alter the composition of the Board and its committees in several respects, as outlined above. Specifically, these changes may improve FINRA's ability to fulfill its mission by modernizing the organization's governance and strengthening the self-regulatory model. This would include increasing access to industry expertise and providing greater flexibility to manage the Board's operations. In particular, the proposed rule change may broaden the range of business models represented on the Board, including those of small firms, and enhance the Board's ability to draw on expertise relevant to evolving market and industry conditions. Greater access to member knowledge, experience and insight may, in turn, support more informed and responsive decision-making.
[
56
]
For the wide range of issues coming before the Board of Governors that are informed by the technical considerations of financial services, the option for broader industry input—over potentially a wider range of perspectives—may lead to better designed regulatory outcomes, enhancing investor protections and market integrity. At the same time, where technical considerations may be of lesser importance, the proposed rule change preserves substantial Public Governor representation that should continue to enable the Board to meet its obligations critical for governance. Greater potential diversity of representation across Industry Governors, combined with the continued substantial Public Governor representation, should serve to mitigate risk that any one set of interests or incentives could predominate in governance. Moreover, Public Governors would continue to have the Chair and a majority on the Audit Committee, providing another important mitigant.
The above discussion about changes in the Board composition also broadly applies to Board committees. While the Board retains oversight of the Board committees' decisions, to the extent that there are resulting shifts in the composition of Board committees, the same considerations related to achieving a mix of industry and public representation apply to Board committees as well.
The existing structural safeguards detailed above would provide additional assurance that FINRA will continue to perform its statutory obligations. Among other things, the composition and responsibilities of offices within FINRA, such as OHO and ODA, that have a high degree of defined independence, would not change. Also, external governance such as comprehensive SEC oversight and the GAO's evaluation of that oversight may complement internal governance.
In addition to the amendments altering the composition of the Board and its committees, the proposed rule change would alter Board structure and continuity. A smaller Board may facilitate coordination and decision-making but may include fewer voices with differing experience and knowledge to address complex issues.
[
57
]
Under the proposed rule change, however, the Board would continue to have a broad range of pertinent expertise and experience. In particular, the conversion of three Industry Governor seats currently reserved for specific segments to at-large seats, as well as the broad expertise residing with Public Governors, may provide the Board greater ability to draw on expertise based on the needs of the organization.
Finally, the number of consecutive three-year terms a Governor may serve would increase from two to three. The additional term may preserve institutional knowledge and Board experience by allowing Governors whose continued service would benefit the Board to serve for another three years.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106867; File No. SR-24X-2026-31]
November 10, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that, on November 3, 2026, 24X National Exchange LLC (“24X” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend 24X Rule 11.14 (“Clearly Erroneous Executions”) in light of the Commission's approval of Overnight Protected Bands for 23/5 Trading. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://equities.24exchange.com/​regulation
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend 24X Rule 11.14 (“Clearly Erroneous Executions”) in light of the Commission's approval of Overnight Protected Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 Trading.
Background
In conjunction with the industry's plans for the introduction of trading 23 hours a day, 5 days a week (“23/5 Trading”), the Operating Committee of the Plan to Address Extraordinary Market Volatility (“LULD Plan”) filed proposed Amendment 27 to the LULD Plan, which proposed to establish price band protections during overnight trading hours (“Overnight Price Bands”).
[
3
]
The Operating Committee proposed that the Overnight Price Bands would initially be temporary static bands 20% above and below two reference points, and that after implementation, the Operating Committee would evaluate the performance of such Overnight Price Bands and propose appropriate changes in a new plan amendment.
[
4
]
On August 5, 2026, the Commission approved the proposal.
[
5
]
In light of the Commission's approval of these changes to the LULD Plan, the Exchange now proposes several amendments to 24X Rule 11.14 regarding Clearly Erroneous Executions. In general, the rule describes the process a market participant may use to request cancellation of a transaction that was “clearly erroneous.” The current rule's central premise is that if LULD Price Bands under the LULD Plan were available and correct at the time the transaction was executed, the transaction is not eligible for clearly erroneous review. Specifically, 24X Rule 11.14(c)(1) currently provides that “[i]f the execution time of the transaction(s) under review is during Regular Trading Hours, the transaction will not be reviewable as clearly erroneous” except in certain limited circumstances, including when (A) the
(
printed page 73363)
transaction is in an NMS stock that is not subject to the LULD Plan (
e.g.,
rights and warrants), (B) the transaction was executed at a time when LULD Price Bands were unavailable or trading should have been prevented due to a regulatory halt or other halt, or (C) several other limited circumstances.
[
6
]
In approving the existing version of the rule, the Commission noted that restricting clearly erroneous review in this way during times when LULD Price Bands were in effect was “consistent with the Act and will further the goal of providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed within the Price Bands will stand and not be broken. . . . Thus, the proposal is designed to limit the potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review process.”
[
7
]
Currently, LULD Price Bands are available only during Regular Trading Hours,
[
8
]
meaning that the restrictions on clearly erroneous review described above apply only during Regular Trading Hours. With the introduction of Overnight Price Bands, the Exchange now proposes to extend the existing restrictions on clearly erroneous review to the period when Overnight Price Bands are in place. This proposed change would be consistent with the Commission's rationale in approving the current version of the rule because it would limit any potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review in the overnight trading session, providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed with the Overnight Price Bands will stand and not be broken.
24X Rule 11.14 currently provides that transactions executed during the 24X Market Session
[
9
]
are treated in the same manner as transactions executed during the Pre-Market
[
10
]
and Post-Market
[
11
]
Sessions. Given the Commission's approval of Overnight Price Bands, the Exchange proposes instead to make clearly erroneous review of transactions executed during the 24X Market Session available in a manner similar to transactions executed during Regular Trading Hours.
Proposed Changes to 24X Rule 11.14(c)(1)
To implement this change, the Exchange proposes to add several definitions to 24X Rule 11.14(c)(1). First, the Exchange would add that the term “LULD Protected Hours” includes Regular Trading Hours and “Overnight Protected Hours” defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan. Second, the Exchange would define “LULD Price Bands” or “Price Bands” to mean the Price Bands defined in Section V of the LULD Plan (
i.e.,
the Price Bands that apply during Regular Trading Hours) and “Overnight Price Bands” as defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan (
i.e.,
the Price Bands that apply to the Overnight Protected Hours from 9:00 p.m. ET through 4:00 a.m. ET).
The Exchange proposes to amend the current first sentence of 24X Rule 11.14(c)(1) to replace the phrase “Regular Trading Hours” with “LULD Protected Hours,” to provide that “[i]f the execution time of the transaction(s) under review is during LULD Protected Hours, the transaction will not be reviewable as clearly erroneous . . . .” This change would extend the LULD-based restrictions on clearly erroneous review currently in place during Regular Trading Hours to the Overnight Protected Hours.
The Exchange also proposes to amend 24X Rule 11.14(c)(1)(B)'s reference to “Percentage Parameter” to incorporate the Percentage Parameter that applies to Overnight Protected Hours. The amended provision would provide for the applicability of clearly erroneous review if the price of the transaction to buy (sell) that is the subject of the clearly erroneous complaint is greater than (less than) the Reference Price by an amount that equals or exceeds the applicable Percentage Parameter defined in Appendix A to the LULD Plan (with respect to the Price Bands that apply during Regular Trading Hours) or the “Overnight Percentage Parameter defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan” (with respect to Overnight Protected Hours).
In addition to these changes, the Exchange also proposes to make a non-substantive change to 24X Rule 11.14(c)(1)(A), substituting the term “LULD Plan” for the current text “the Plan to Address Extraordinary Market Volatility Pursuant to Rule 608 of Regulation NMS under the Act (the `Limit Up-Limit Down Plan' or `LULD Plan,')” as the “LULD Plan” would be defined in the proposed revision to 24X Rule 11.14(c)(1).
Proposed Changes to 24X Rule 11.14(c)(2), (d)(3), and (f)
As noted above, current 24X Rule 11.14(c)(1)(A) permits clearly erroneous review even during Regular Trading Hours when the transaction in question is in an NMS Stock that is not subject to the LULD Plan,
i.e.,
rights and warrants. Such transactions are reviewed for clearly erroneous status using the procedures set out in 24X Rule 11.14(c)(2), including the Numerical Guidelines set out in the table accompanying 24X Rule 11.14(c)(2)(A). The Exchange now proposes to introduce a similar provision regarding transactions in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan that are executed during the Overnight Protected Hours; such transactions would be subject to the same Numerical Guidelines as transactions occurring in the Pre-Market Session and Post-Market Session.
The heading of 24X Rule 11.14(c)(2) addresses “[r]eview of transactions occurring during Pre-Market Session, Post Market Session, 24X Market Session, or eligible for review pursuant to paragraph (c)(1)(A).” The Exchange proposes to remove the reference to the 24X Market Session and replace the phrase “eligible for review pursuant to paragraph (c)(1)(A)” (which, in the current rule, means transactions executed during Regular Trading Hours in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan) with “during LULD Protected Hours in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan.” This proposed language would cover transactions in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan in Regular Trading Hours and expand the same treatment to transactions executed in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan during Overnight Protected Hours. As such, the proposed change is not novel.
The Exchange proposes to make the same change everywhere else such language appears in the rule—namely, in the text of paragraphs (c)(2)(A), (c)(2)(B), (c)(2)(C), (c)(2)(D),
[
12
]
(d)(3), and (f).
[
13
]
In each case, the Exchange proposes to remove the reference to the
(
printed page 73364)
24X Market Session and replace the phrase “eligible for review pursuant to paragraph (c)(1)(A)” with “during LULD Protected Hours in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan.”
The Exchange also proposes to make corresponding changes to the headings of the table accompanying 24X Rule 11.14(c)(2)(A). The Exchange proposes to change the heading of the second column from “Core Market Session
[
14
]
Numerical Guidelines for transactions eligible for review pursuant to paragraph (c)(1)(A)” to “Numerical Guidelines for Transactions Executed During the Core Market Session in NMS Stocks Not Subject to the LULD Plan.” This change would simply replace the shorthand “eligible for review pursuant to paragraph (c)(1)(A)” with the fuller description that such transactions are “executed during the Core Market Session in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan,” and is not a substantive change.
Similarly, the Exchange proposes to change the heading of the third column from “Pre-Market, Post-Market Session and 24X Market Session Numerical Guidelines” to “Numerical Guidelines for Transactions Executed During the Pre-Market and Post-Market Session or during Overnight Protected Hours in NMS Stocks Not Subject to the LULD Plan.” The proposed change removes the reference to the 24X Market Session and addresses the fact that transactions executed during Overnight Protected Hours in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan are eligible for clearly erroneous review—just as are transactions in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan executed during Regular Trading Hours—but at the Numerical Guidelines that apply outside of Regular Trading Hours.
Together, these proposed changes would extend the eligibility of clearly erroneous review for transactions in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan that is currently in place during Regular Trading Hours to the Overnight Protected Hours, and would apply the Commission's recent approval of Overnight Price Bands to the clearly erroneous executions rule.
Implementation
The Exchange understands that the other national securities exchanges and FINRA will also file similar proposals, the substance of which are identical to this proposal. The Exchange proposes that this rule change would become operative at the commencement of 23/5 Trading, which is scheduled to commence industry-wide on December 6, 2026.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder that are applicable to a national securities exchange, and, in particular, with the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
15
]
Specifically, the proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
16
]
because it would promote just and equitable principles of trade, remove impediments to, and perfect the mechanism of, a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, protect investors and the public interest.
The Exchange believes that the proposed change is consistent with just and equitable principles of trade because it extends the basic premise of the current rule that clearly erroneous review should be generally unavailable any time a transaction is executed within LULD Price Bands at a time the Price Bands were available and correct. Currently, LULD Price Bands are available only during Regular Trading Hours, meaning that the restrictions on clearly erroneous review described above apply only during Regular Trading Hours. With the introduction of Overnight Price Bands, the Exchange believes that removing former references to the 24X Market Session and extending such restrictions on clearly erroneous review to the period when Overnight Price Bands are in place would remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system by enhancing the transparency and consistency of the rule.
The resulting rule would thus extend the LULD-related limits on clearly erroneous review that are applicable in Regular Trading Hours to the overnight period. The proposed change would also be consistent with the Commission's rationale in approving the current version of the rule because it would limit any potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review in the overnight trading session, providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed with the Overnight Price Bands will stand and not be broken.
[
17
]
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange believes the proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(8) of the Act
[
18
]
in that it does not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Rather than impacting competition, the proposed change would simply extend the basic premise of the current rule that clearly erroneous review should be generally unavailable any time a transaction is executed within LULD Price Bands at a time the Price Bands were available and correct. The Exchange understands that the other national securities exchanges and FINRA will also file similar proposals, the substance of which are identical to this proposal. Thus, the proposed rule change will help to ensure consistency across SROs without implicating any competitive issues.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
19
]
and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
[
20
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings
(
printed page 73365)
to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-24X-2026-31 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-24X-2026-31. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-24X-2026-31 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
21
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106866; File No. SR-TXSE-2026-045]
November 10, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 9, 2026, Texas Stock Exchange LLC (the “Exchange” or “TXSE”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II, below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to adopt a policy relating to the Exchange's treatment of trade reports that it determines to be inconsistent with the prevailing market. The proposed rule change is available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
) at the Exchange's website (
https://www.txse.com/​regulations/​rules-filings
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
(
printed page 73313)
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
Trades in listed securities occasionally occur at prices that deviate from prevailing market prices, and those trades sometimes establish a high, low or last sale price for a security that does not reflect its true market. The Consolidated Tape Association (“CTA”) Plan and the Nasdaq UTP Plan (“UTP Plan”) each offer participants in such plans with the discretion to append an Aberrant Report Indicator to a trade report to indicate that the market believes that the trade price of a particular trade executed on the participant's market does not accurately reflect the prevailing market for the security in question.
[
3
]
Several national securities exchanges, including The New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”)
[
4
]
and Nasdaq Stock Market (“Nasdaq”),
[
5
]
and more recently, Investors Exchange LLC (“IEX”)
[
6
]
and NYSE Texas, Inc. (“NYSE Texas”),
[
7
]
have adopted policies related to use of the Aberrant Report Indicator for equities trades that, while not eligible for cancellation pursuant to applicable exchange rules governing clearly erroneous executions, are determined not to accurately reflect the prevailing market for the security in question. The Exchange believes that such policies are appropriate to identify such trades to vendors and market participants so that they may exclude such trades from relevant pricing metrics (
e.g.,
high, low and last sale prices). Accordingly, TXSE is proposing to adopt a policy substantially similar to the existing policies of such other national securities exchanges as described below.
[
8
]
During the course of surveillance by the Exchange or as a result of notification by another market, listed company,
[
9
]
or market participant, the Exchange may become aware of trade prices that do not accurately reflect the prevailing market for a particular security. In such a case, the Exchange will contact the listing exchange (if the Exchange is not the listing exchange) and other markets (in the case of executions that take place across multiple markets) to seek consensus as to whether the trade price is consistent with the prevailing market for the security. If the Exchange determines that the trade price is inconsistent with the prevailing market for the security after considering the factors discussed below, the Exchange will append an Aberrant Report Indicator to the trade pursuant to applicable CTA and UTP procedures. Appending an Aberrant Report Indicator to the trade will have no effect on the validity of the underlying trade.
The proposed policy would be applicable to trades that occur on TXSE, whether traded on an unlisted trading privilege (“UTP”) basis or listed on TXSE.
In making the determination to append the Aberrant Report Indicator to a particular trade, the Exchange shall consider all factors related to a trade, including, but not limited to, the following:
Material news released for the security;
Suspicious trading activity;
System malfunctions or disruptions;
Locked or crossed markets;
A recent trading halt or resumption of trading in the security;
Whether the security is in its initial public offering;
Volume and volatility for the security;
Whether the trade represents a 52-week high or low for the security;
Whether the trade price deviates significantly from recent trading patterns in the security;
Whether the trade price reflects a stock-split, reorganization or other corporate action;
The validity of consolidated tape trades and quotes in comparison to national best bids and offers; and
The general volatility of market conditions.
In determining whether trade prices are inconsistent with the prevailing market, the Exchange proposes that its policy shall be to follow the following general guidelines: The Exchange will review whether a trade price does not reflect the prevailing market for a security if the trade occurs during regular trading hours (
i.e.,
9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.) and occurs at a price that deviates from the “Reference Price” by an amount that meets or exceeds the following thresholds:
Trade price
Numerical
                             threshold 
                             (percent)
Between $0 and $15.00
7
Between $15.01 and $50.00
5
In excess of $50.00
3
The “Reference Price” refers to (a) if the primary market for the security is open at the time of the trade, the national best bid or offer for the security, or (b) if the primary market for the security is not open at the time of the trade, the first executable quote or print for the security on the primary market after execution of the trade in question. However, if the circumstances suggest that a different Reference Price would be more appropriate, the Exchange will use the different Reference Price. For instance, if the national best bid and offer for the security are so wide apart as to fail to reflect the market for the security, the Exchange might use as the Reference Price a trade price or best bid or offer that was available prior to the trade in question.
If TXSE determines that a trade price does not reflect the prevailing market for a security and the trade represented the last sale of the security on the Exchange during a trading session, the Exchange may also determine to remove that trade's designation as the last sale and the preceding last sale eligible trade would become the new last sale. TXSE may do so either on the day of the trade or at a later date, so as to provide reasonable time for the Exchange to conduct due diligence regarding the trade, including the consideration of
(
printed page 73314)
input from markets and other market participants.
In connection with the proposed policy, TXSE shall discourage vendors and other data recipients from using prices to which the Exchange has appended the Aberrant Report Indicator in any calculation of the high, low or last sale price of a security; and will urge vendors to disclose the exclusion from high, low or last sale price data of any trades with an Aberrant Report Indicator and exclude them from high, low or last sale price information they disseminate and to provide to data users an explanation of the parameters used in the Exchange's aberrant trade policy.
[
10
]
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
11
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
12
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
In particular, and as described in rule change proposals of NYSE, Nasdaq, IEX, and NYSE Texas to adopt a policy on the use of the Aberrant Report Indicator, the Exchange believes that the Aberrant Report Indicator is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest in that the Exchange will seek to ensure a proper understanding of the Aberrant Report Indicator among securities market participants by: (i) urging vendors to disclose the exclusion from high, low or last sale price data of any aberrant trades excluded from high, low or last sale price information they disseminate and to provide to data users an explanation of the parameters used in the Exchange's aberrant trade policy; (ii) informing the affected listed company each time the Exchange or another market appends the Aberrant Report Indicator to an Exchange-listed stock; and (iii) reminding the users of the information that these are still valid trades in that they were executed and not unwound as in the case of a clearly erroneous trade.
Additionally, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is a reasonable means to alert investors and others that the Exchange believes that the trade price for a particular trade executed in its market does not accurately reflect the prevailing market for the security. Further, the Exchange will use the same factors, including objective numerical thresholds in determining whether a trade report is eligible to have an Aberrant Report Indicator appended to it. As discussed above, other national securities exchanges have adopted a substantially similar policy. Accordingly, the proposed rule change does not raise any new or novel issues that have not already been considered by the Commission.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
TXSE does not believe that the proposed rule change will result in any burden on competition. The proposed rule change is designed to enable the Exchange to apply the Aberrant Report Indicator in a manner consistent with its existing use by other national securities exchanges, thereby increasing transparency regarding trades executed at prices that do not reflect the prevailing market, and not to address any competitive issues. The Exchange will utilize the indicator in a consistent manner with respect to all Exchange members and listed companies. The Exchange thus does not believe the proposal will burden competition because it will provide for consistency between the Exchange's policy related to use of the Aberrant Report Indicator and those of other national securities exchanges.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received written comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
13
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
14
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii) thereunder.
[
15
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act
[
16
]
to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include File Number SR-TXSE-2026-045 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to File Number SR-TXSE-2026-045. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may
(
printed page 73315)
redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-045 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
17
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.
