Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106865; File No. SR-NASDAQ-2026-096]
November 10, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”,
[
1
]
) and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 2, 2026, The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III, below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend Section 115(f)(3) of Equity 7 to provide that the Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure subscription service is available to support only Day Session ports, and not ports to be used in the Night Session, as described below.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​nasdaq/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Section 115(f)(3) of Equity 7 (Pricing Schedule) to provide that the Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure subscription service offered under that provision is available to support Day Session
[
3
]
ports only and is not available to support Night Session
[
4
]
ports.
The Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure service allows a member firm to assign up to 30 of its OUCH ports to a dedicated server infrastructure for its exclusive use.
[
5
]
An OUCH port is a connectivity port designated to accept only OUCH protocol messaging, which provides a method for subscribers to send orders and receive status updates on those orders.
A Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure subscription is available to a member
(
printed page 73321)
firm for a fee of $5,000 per month, which is in addition to the standard fees assessed for each OUCH port. A one-time installation fee of $5,000 is assessed to subscribers for each Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure subscription. The service is optional and is available to all member firms.
[
6
]
Absent a subscription, the Exchange distributes a member firm's OUCH ports among shared servers, which act as switches that channel the message traffic a member firm sends through its ports to the Exchange's system. All port servers, including the servers used for the Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure service, are owned and operated by the Exchange, and a subscribing member firm does not have physical access to its dedicated server or the ability to modify it.
The Exchange now proposes to amend Section 115(f)(3) of Equity 7 to provide that the Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure subscription service is available to support Day Session ports only and is not available to support Night Session ports.
[
7
]
The reason for the proposed change is that the Exchange has determined that separating the operation of Day Session ports and Night Session ports, as proposed, is appropriate to facilitate the orderly maintenance and operation of its ports generally.
[
8
]
The Exchange therefore proposes to state expressly in its rules that the Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure service supports Day Session ports only, and that the offering is not available to support Night Session ports.
[
9
]
The Exchange anticipates that fewer than ten subscribers will be affected by the proposed rule change. To continue using their Night Session ports, each affected subscriber need only place its Night Session ports on shared server infrastructure at no additional cost, as Exchange customers that do not subscribe to the Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure subscription service do today. Night Session OUCH ports placed on shared servers will remain subject to the fees otherwise applicable to OUCH ports under Section 115 of Equity 7.
[
10
]
The Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure subscription service, including its fees, will continue to be available to support Day Session ports without change.
The Exchange proposes to make the proposed rule change effective upon filing and operative on November 2, 2026, so that the Exchange provide timely notice to subscribers of the service.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
11
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
12
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is reasonable. The Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure subscription service is optional, and a subscriber will continue to receive the same service for the same subscription fee in support of its Day Session ports. The Exchange has determined that separating the operation of Day Session and Night Session ports is appropriate to facilitate the orderly maintenance and operation of its ports generally. Thus, the Exchange proposes to specify that the Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure subscription service is available for Day Session ports only and that the service is not available to support the use of Night Session ports. The Exchange notes that Night Session ports remain subject to the fees otherwise applicable to OUCH ports under Section 115 of Equity 7.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is an equitable allocation of fees and is not unfairly discriminatory. The proposal applies uniformly to all member firms and turns on the trading session the optional connectivity offering supports, not on the identity of the member firm. Every member firm will connect its Night Session ports in the same manner, whether or not it subscribes to the service for its Day Session ports.
The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule change promotes just and equitable principles of trade and removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system by stating clearly in its rules which ports the service supports, so that member firms can arrange their Night Session connectivity accordingly.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose a burden on intramarket competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure service is optional, and the proposal will apply equally to every member firm that subscribes to it. Every member firm, including a subscriber to the service, may place its Night Session ports on shared server infrastructure, which is how most customers connect to the Exchange today.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose a burden on intermarket competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposal addresses only which ports an optional connectivity service—the Dedicated OUCH Infrastructure subscription service—supports. Member firms are not required to use the Dedicated OUCH Port Infrastructure service to access the Exchange.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act.
[
13
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is: (i) necessary or appropriate in the public interest; (ii) for the protection of investors; or (iii) otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
(
printed page 73322)
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NASDAQ-2026-096 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NASDAQ-2026-096. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NASDAQ-2026-096 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
14
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; MEMX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Exchange's Fee Schedule
full_text:

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106864; File No. SR-MEMX-2026-34]
November 10, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 30, 2026, MEMX LLC (“MEMX” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange is filing with the Commission a proposed rule change to amend the Exchange's fee schedule
(
printed page 73282)
applicable to Members
[
3
]
(the “Fee Schedule”) pursuant to Exchange Rules 15.1(a) and (c). As is further described below, the Exchange proposes to: (i) adopt a new DLI Tier 1 and re-designate the existing DLI Tiers 1 and 2 as DLI Tiers 2 and 3, respectively; and (ii) provide that the additive rebates under the Tape A Quoting Tier, Tape B Volume Tier 1, Tape B Volume Tier 2, and Tape C Quoting Tier are not eligible to be combined with any DLI Tier rebate. The Exchange proposes to implement the changes to the Fee Schedule pursuant to this proposal on November 2, 2026. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The purpose of the proposed rule change is to amend the Fee Schedule to: (i) adopt a new DLI Tier 1 and re-designate the existing DLI Tiers 1 and 2 as DLI Tiers 2 and 3, respectively; and (ii) provide that the additive rebates under the Tape A Quoting Tier, Tape B Volume Tier 1, Tape B Volume Tier 2, and Tape C Quoting Tier are not eligible to be combined with any DLI Tier rebate, each as further described below.
The Exchange first notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient. More specifically, the Exchange is only one of 18 registered equities exchanges, as well as a number of alternative trading systems and other off-exchange venues, to which market participants may direct their order flow. Based on publicly available information, no single registered equities exchange currently has more than approximately 14% of the total market share of executed volume of equities trading.
[
4
]
Thus, in such a low-concentrated and highly competitive market, no single equities exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of order flow, and the Exchange currently represents approximately 1.6% of the overall market share.
[
5
]
The Exchange in particular operates a “Maker-Taker” model whereby it provides rebates to Members that add liquidity to the Exchange and charges fees to Members that remove liquidity from the Exchange. The Fee Schedule sets forth the standard rebates and fees applied per share for orders that add and remove liquidity, respectively. Additionally, in response to the competitive environment, the Exchange also offers tiered pricing, which provides Members with opportunities to qualify for higher rebates or lower fees where certain volume criteria and thresholds are met. Tiered pricing provides an incremental incentive for Members to strive for higher tier levels, which provides increasingly higher benefits or discounts for satisfying increasingly more stringent criteria.
Currently, the Exchange provides a standard rebate of $0.0015 per share for executions of orders in securities priced at or above $1.00 per share that add displayed liquidity to the Exchange (such orders, “Added Displayed Volume”).
[
6
]
The Exchange also offers enhanced rebates for executions of Added Displayed Volume under the Displayed Liquidity Incentive (“DLI”) Tiers, as well as additive rebates for qualifying executions of Added Displayed Volume in Tape A, Tape B and Tape C securities, each as described below.
Adoption of New DLI Tier 1 and Re-Designation of Existing DLI Tiers
The Exchange currently offers DLI Tiers 1 and 2 under which a Member may receive an enhanced rebate for executions of Added Displayed Volume by achieving the corresponding required criteria for each such tier. The DLI Tiers are designed to encourage Members, through the provision of an enhanced rebate for executions of Added Displayed Volume, to promote price discovery and market quality by quoting at the NBBO for a significant portion of each day (
i.e.,
through the applicable quoting requirement
[
7
]
) in a broad base of securities (
i.e.,
through the applicable securities requirement
[
8
]
), thereby benefitting the Exchange and investors by providing improved trading conditions for all market participants through narrower bid-ask spreads and increased depth of liquidity available at the NBBO in a broad base of securities and committing capital to support the execution of orders.
Currently, under DLI Tier 1, the Exchange provides an enhanced rebate of $0.0032 per share for executions of Added Displayed Volume for Members that qualify for such tier by achieving an NBBO Time of at least 50% in an average of at least 1,000 securities per trading day during the month. Under DLI Tier 2, the Exchange currently provides an enhanced rebate of $0.0026 per share for executions of Added Displayed Volume for Members that qualify for such tier by achieving an NBBO Time of at least 25% in an average of at least 500 securities per trading day during the month.
The Exchange now proposes to adopt a new DLI Tier 1 under which the Exchange would provide an enhanced rebate of $0.0035 per share for executions of Added Displayed Volume for Members that qualify for such tier by achieving an NBBO Time of at least 50% in an average of at least 1,300 securities per trading day during the month. In connection with the adoption of the proposed new DLI Tier 1, the Exchange proposes to re-designate the existing DLI Tier 1 as DLI Tier 2 and the existing DLI Tier 2 as DLI Tier 3. The rebates and the required criteria under the re-designated DLI Tiers 2 and 3 are not changing, and the pricing under such tiers would continue to be available to Members on the same terms as it is today.
[
9
]
In addition, the Exchange
(
printed page 73283)
is not proposing to change the rebate provided under any DLI Tier for executions of orders in securities priced below $1.00 per share, which would continue to be 0.15% of the total dollar value of the transaction.
The proposed new DLI Tier 1 is designed to reward Members that quote at the NBBO for a significant portion of each day in a broader set of securities than is currently required under any DLI Tier. Specifically, the securities requirement under the proposed new DLI Tier 1 (1,300 securities) is 300 securities greater than the securities requirement under the existing DLI Tier 1 (which would become DLI Tier 2), while the quoting requirement (50%) is the same. In exchange for meeting these more stringent criteria, the Exchange proposes to provide a rebate that is $0.0003 per share higher than the rebate provided under the existing DLI Tier 1. The Exchange believes that the proposed new DLI Tier 1 would encourage Members to quote at the NBBO in a broader base of securities, thereby benefitting investors by providing improved trading conditions for all market participants through narrower bid-ask spreads and increased depth of liquidity available at the NBBO in a larger number of securities.
Tape Specific Additive Rebates
The Exchange currently offers four additive rebates for a qualifying Members' executions of Added Displayed Volume (other than Retail Orders
[
10
]
) in Tape A, Tape B or Tape C securities priced over $1.00 per share: (i) the Tape A Quoting Tier, which provides an additive rebate of $0.0001 per share for Members that achieve an NBBO Time of at least 25% in an average of at least 500 Tape A securities per trading day during the month; (ii) the Tape B Volume Tier 1, which provides an additive rebate of $0.0004 per share for Members that achieve certain Tape B and Non-Display volume criteria; (iii) the Tape B Volume Tier 2, which provides an additive rebate of $0.0002 per share for Members that achieve certain Tape B volume criteria; and (iv) the Tape C Quoting Tier, which provides an additive rebate of $0.0001 per share for Members that achieve an NBBO Time of at least 50% in an average of at least 500 Tape C securities per trading day during the month (together, the “Tape-Specific Additive Rebates”).
[
11
]
Currently, each Tape-Specific Additive Rebate is provided in addition to the otherwise applicable rebates for qualifying executions, including the enhanced rebates under the DLI Tiers.
The Exchange now proposes to provide that the Tape-Specific Additive Rebates are not eligible to be combined with any DLI Tier rebate. Accordingly, an execution of Added Displayed Volume that receives a rebate under a DLI Tier would not also receive a Tape-Specific Additive Rebate. The Exchange is not proposing to change the amount of, or the required criteria for, any Tape-Specific Additive Rebate, and is not proposing any change to the NBBO Setter additive rebate.
[
12
]
The Exchange believes that the DLI Tiers and the Tape-Specific Additive Rebates provide different incentives to quote aggressively. The DLI Tiers provide an incentive to quote at the NBBO across a broad base of securities, regardless of Tape, whereas the Tape-Specific Additive Rebates are designed for Members that target quoting (or, in the case of the Tape B Volume Tiers, volume) in securities of a particular Tape. The Exchange believes that not permitting these incentives to be combined will better differentiate them and allow each to serve its distinct purpose. Additionally, because the Exchange is proposing to adopt a new DLI Tier 1 under which Members may earn rebates of up to $0.0035 per share, the Exchange is also proposing this change to control the costs associated with its transaction pricing, including the rebates it provides for liquidity-adding orders, in a manner that is still consistent with the Exchange's overall pricing philosophy of encouraging added liquidity and promoting the price discovery and market quality objectives of the DLI Tiers described above.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6 of the Act,
[
13
]
in general, and with Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
14
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
As discussed above, the Exchange operates in a highly fragmented and competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient, and the Exchange represents only a small percentage of the overall market. The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and also recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
15
]
The Exchange believes that the ever-shifting market share among the exchanges from month to month demonstrates that market participants can shift order flow or discontinue use of certain categories of products, in response to new or different pricing structures being introduced into the market. Accordingly, competitive forces constrain the Exchange's transaction fees and rebates, and market participants can readily trade on competing venues if they deem pricing levels at those other venues to be more favorable. The Exchange believes the proposal reflects a reasonable and competitive pricing structure designed to incentivize market participants to direct additional order flow, including displayed, liquidity-adding orders to the Exchange, which the Exchange believes would promote price discovery and enhance liquidity and market quality on
(
printed page 73284)
the Exchange to the benefit of all Members and market participants.
The Exchange believes that the proposed new DLI Tier 1 is reasonable, equitable and not unfairly discriminatory for these same reasons. The DLI Tiers, like the Exchange's other volume and quoting-based incentives, are available to all Members on an equal basis and provide additional benefits that are reasonably related to the value to an exchange's market quality associated with higher levels of quoting activity. The proposed new DLI Tier 1 is designed to encourage Members to quote at the NBBO for a significant portion of each day in a broader base of securities, which the Exchange believes would promote price discovery and enhance liquidity and market quality on the Exchange to the benefit of all Members and market participants. The Exchange believes that the proposed rebate of $0.0035 per share is commensurate with the more stringent required criteria under the proposed new DLI Tier 1, as such criteria would require a Member to quote at the NBBO in an average of at least 300 more securities per day than is required under the existing highest DLI Tier, and is reasonably related to the market quality benefits that such tier is designed to achieve. The Exchange also believes the proposal is reasonable because the proposed new DLI Tier 1 is comparable in structure to quoting-based tiers offered by other exchanges, which provide enhanced rebates to members that quote at the NBBO for a specified portion of the trading day in a specified number of securities.
[
16
]
The Exchange notes that the proposed securities requirement of 1,300 securities is higher than the securities requirements under the quoting tiers cited above, and the proposed rebate is calibrated to the more stringent criteria.
The Exchange believes that the proposed re-designation of the existing DLI Tiers 1 and 2 as DLI Tiers 2 and 3, respectively, is reasonable, equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it is a non-substantive change that does not alter the rebate or the required criteria under either tier, and it ensures that the DLI Tiers are numbered in descending order of rebate and required criteria, which the Exchange believes provides clarity and transparency to Members. The re-designated tiers will continue to be available to all Members on an equal basis.
The Exchange believes that the proposed change to provide that the Tape-Specific Additive Rebates are not eligible to be combined with any DLI Tier rebate is reasonable because it differentiates between the incentives offered under the DLI Tiers, which are designed to encourage quoting at the NBBO across a broad base of securities, and the Tape-Specific Additive Rebates, which are designed for Members that target quoting or volume in securities of a particular Tape. The Exchange also believes the change is reasonable because it will help the Exchange control the costs of its pricing structure in light of the higher rebates available under the DLI Tiers, including under the proposed new DLI Tier 1. The Exchange notes that other exchanges similarly limit the ability of members to combine enhanced quoting-based rebates with certain additive rebates.
[
17
]
The Exchange believes the proposed change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it applies uniformly to all Members, and all Members remain eligible to qualify for the DLI Tiers and the Tape-Specific Additive Rebates in accordance with the criteria for each.
For the reasons discussed above, the Exchange submits that the proposal satisfies the requirements of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
18
]
in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities and is not designed to unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. As described more fully below in the Exchange's statement regarding the burden on competition, the Exchange believes that its transaction pricing is subject to significant competitive forces, and that the proposed fees described herein are appropriate to address such forces.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposal will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Instead, as discussed above, the proposal is intended to incentivize market participants to direct additional order flow to the Exchange, thereby enhancing liquidity and market quality on the Exchange to the benefit of all Members and market participants. As a result, the Exchange believes the proposal would enhance its competitiveness as a market that attracts actionable orders, thereby making it a more desirable destination venue for its customers. For these reasons, the Exchange believes that the proposal furthers the Commission's goal in adopting Regulation NMS of fostering competition among orders, which promotes “more efficient pricing of individual stocks for all types of orders, large and small.”
[
19
]
Intramarket Competition
As discussed above, the Exchange believes that the proposed new DLI Tier 1 would incentivize Members to quote at the NBBO in a broader base of securities, thereby enhancing liquidity and market quality on the Exchange to the benefit of all Members, as well as enhancing the attractiveness of the Exchange as a trading venue, which the Exchange believes, in turn, would continue to encourage market participants to direct additional order flow to the Exchange. Greater liquidity benefits all Members by providing more trading opportunities and encourages Members to send additional orders to the Exchange, thereby contributing to robust levels of liquidity, which benefits all market participants.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed changes would impose any burden on intramarket competition because such changes will apply to all Members uniformly. The opportunity to qualify for the proposed new DLI Tier 1 and the re-designated DLI Tiers 2 and 3 is available to all Members, as is the opportunity to qualify for each of the Tape-Specific Additive Rebates, and the proposed limitation on combining the Tape-Specific Additive Rebates with DLI Tier rebates would apply equally to all Members. As described above, the Exchange believes that the required criteria under the proposed new DLI Tier 1 is commensurate with the corresponding rebate and reasonably related to the enhanced liquidity and
(
printed page 73285)
market quality that such tier is designed to promote. For the foregoing reasons, the Exchange believes the proposed changes would not impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
Intermarket Competition
As noted above, the Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient. Members have numerous alternative venues that they may participate on and direct their order flow to, including 17 other equities exchanges and numerous alternative trading systems and other off-exchange venues. As noted above, no single registered equities exchange currently has more than approximately 14% of the total market share of executed volume of equities trading. Thus, in such a low-concentrated and highly competitive market, no single equities exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of order flow. Moreover, the Exchange believes that the ever-shifting market share among the exchanges from month to month demonstrates that market participants can shift order flow or reduce use of certain categories of products, in response to new or different pricing structures being introduced into the market. Accordingly, competitive forces constrain the Exchange's transaction fees and rebates, including with respect to Added Displayed Volume and market participants can readily choose to send their orders to other exchange and off-exchange venues if they deem fee levels at those other venues to be more favorable. As described above, the proposed changes represent a competitive proposal through which the Exchange is seeking to encourage the submission of additional order flow to the Exchange through volume and quoting-based tiers, which have been widely adopted by exchanges, including the Exchange, while also controlling the costs associated with its transaction pricing. Accordingly, the Exchange believes the proposal would not burden, but rather promote, intermarket competition by enabling it to better compete with other exchanges that offer similar pricing incentives to market participants.
Additionally, the Commission has repeatedly expressed its preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. Specifically, in Regulation NMS, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
20
]
The fact that this market is competitive has also long been recognized by the courts. In
NetCoalition
v.
SEC,
the D.C. Circuit stated as follows: “[n]o one disputes that competition for order flow is `fierce.' . . . As the SEC explained, `[i]n the U.S. national market system, buyers and sellers of securities, and the broker-dealers that act as their order-routing agents, have a wide range of choices of where to route orders for execution'; [and] `no exchange can afford to take its market share percentages for granted' because `no exchange possesses a monopoly, regulatory or otherwise, in the execution of order flow from broker dealers'. . . .”.
[
21
]
Accordingly, the Exchange does not believe its proposed pricing changes impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act
[
22
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2)
[
23
]
thereunder.
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
