Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106860; File No. SR-ISE-2026-57]
November 9, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 27, 2026, Nasdaq ISE, LLC (“ISE” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the fees for Nasdaq 100® Index (“NDX”)
[
3
]
options in the Exchange's Pricing Schedule at Options 7, Section 5.A.
While the changes proposed herein are effective upon filing, the Exchange has designated the amendments become operative on November 1, 2026.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​ise/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to increase the NDX and NDXP options fees for regular orders assessed to Non-Priority Customer
[
4
]
market participants in Options 7, Section 5.A. The Exchange also proposes some minor technical amendments to the Pricing Schedule. The changes are described below.
As set forth in Options 7, Section 5.A, the Exchange currently assesses a fee of $0.75 per contract for NDX and NDXP
(
printed page 73335)
Market Maker,
[
5
]
Non-Nasdaq ISE Market Maker (FarMM),
[
6
]
Firm Proprietary
[
7
]
/Broker-Dealer
[
8
]
and Professional Customer
[
9
]
regular orders. Priority Customer
[
10
]
orders are currently assessed a $0.50 per contract fee in NDX and NDXP.
The Exchange now proposes to increase the Non-Priority Customer NDX fees for regular orders from $0.75 to $1.25 per contract. As a result, Non-Priority Customer orders would each be assessed a fee of $1.25 per contract in NDX and NDXP. The Exchange is not proposing to amend the Priority Customer fee of $0.50 per contract in NDX or NDXP, or the fees for other index options in Options 7, Section 5.
The notes to Options 7, Section 5.A would continue to apply, unchanged. Specifically: (i) note 1 provides that, for all executions in complex NDX (and NDXP)
[
11
]
orders for Non-Priority Customers, the applicable complex order fees for Non-Select Symbols in Options 7, Section 4 will apply, and for all executions in complex NDX (and NDXP)
[
12
]
orders for Priority Customers, the fee will be $0.25 per contract; (ii) note 2 provides that a surcharge of $0.25 per contract is assessed to all Priority Customer complex executions in NDX (and NDXP);
[
13
]
(iii) note 3 provides that a surcharge of $0.25 per contract is assessed to all market participants for simple and complex executions in NDX (and NDXP)
[
14
]
with a premium price of $25.00 or greater; and (iv) note 4 provides that a surcharge is assessed to electronic simple Non-Priority Customer orders in NDX and NDXP that remove liquidity according to a premium schedule, which ranges from $1.00 per contract for premiums of less than $3.00 to $3.00 per contract for premiums greater than or equal to $50.00. Because complex NDX orders for Non-Priority Customers are assessed the Non-Select Symbol complex order fees in Options 7, Section 4 pursuant to note 1, the proposed fee increase would apply to Non-Priority Customer regular (simple) orders in NDX.
By way of example, under the proposed pricing a Market Maker electronic simple order in NDX with a premium of $5.00 that adds liquidity would be assessed $1.50 per contract ($1.25 fee plus the $0.25 per contract surcharge in section 5.D), as compared to $1.00 per contract today ($0.75 fee plus the $0.25 per contract surcharge in section 5.D). If the same order removed liquidity, it would be assessed $3.00 per contract (the $1.25 fee, the $0.25 per contract surcharge in section 5.D, plus the $1.50 note 4 surcharge), as compared to $2.50 per contract today (the $0.75 fee, the $0.25 per contract surcharge in section 5.D, plus the $1.50 note 4 surcharge). A Professional Customer simple order in NDX with a premium of $30.00 that adds liquidity would be assessed $1.75 per contract (the $1.25 fee plus the $0.25 surcharge in section 5.D plus the $0.25 note 3 surcharge) as compared to $1.25 per contract today (the $0.75 fee plus the $0.25 surcharge in section 5.D plus the $0.25 note 3 surcharge). By comparison, a Priority Customer simple order in NDX that adds liquidity with a premium of $30.00 would continue to be assessed $0.75 per contract (the $0.50 fee plus the $0.25 note 3 surcharge).
While the Exchange is increasing the NDX and NDXP Non-Priority Customer fee, the Exchange believes that market participants will continue to transact NDX and NDXP options on ISE given the large notional value of NDX. Each options contract has a multiplier of $100, so a single contract represents notional exposure equal to $100 times the index level. For example, at an index level of 20,000, one NDX contract represents approximately $2,000,000 in notional value. At that level, the proposed $1.25 per contract fee represents approximately 0.00625 basis points of notional value, and the proposed $0.50 increase represents approximately 0.0025 basis points. Because the Exchange's fees are assessed per contract regardless of the size of the underlying exposure, the cost of the fee relative to the economic exposure obtained is small. It remains small even after the proposed increase. The Exchange notes that the increase is modest relative to the value of the exposure each NDX contract provides.
The Exchange's proposal to note “and NDXP” in a few places in Options 7, Section 5,A. is a non-substantive change as “NDX” is defined to include a.m.-settled and p.m.-settled on NDX options. Adding NDXP will bring greater visibility to the rule text and conform the text.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
15
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
16
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes that its proposal to increase the Non-Priority Customer NDX and NDXP fees for regular orders from $0.75 to $1.25 per contract is reasonable because Priority Customers will continue to be assessed a lower fee as compared to Non-Priority Customers, and the existing notes and surcharges in NDX and NDXP will continue to apply unchanged. The Exchange believes that, even with the increase, Non-Priority Customer pricing in NDX and NDXP will remain competitive and will continue to attract order flow to the Exchange.
The Exchange believes that the proposed Non-Priority Customer fee of $1.25 per contract in NDX and NDXP options is reasonable when considered in relation to the notional value of the product. Each NDX options contract has a multiplier of $100, so a single contract represents notional exposure equal to $100 times the index level.
[
17
]
Because the Exchange's options fees are assessed per contract regardless of the size of the underlying exposure, the cost of the fee relative to the economic exposure obtained is small. It remains small even after the proposed increase. Viewed another way, a market participant seeking comparable Nasdaq 100 exposure through other products would generally need to trade many more contracts, each of which is subject to its own transaction fees. For example, a market participant seeking exposure equivalent to one NDX contract through
(
printed page 73336)
options overlying Invesco QQQ Trust (“QQQ”)
[
18
]
would need to trade approximately 41 QQQ options contracts. Those contracts would be subject to per-contract transaction fees of up to $0.45 each on the Exchange for an aggregate cost of approximately $18.45. On a notional-equivalent basis, therefore, the proposed NDX and NDXP options fees remain lower than the cost of obtaining similar exposure through alternative products. The Exchange also notes that the proposed fee is lower in some cases and higher in other cases than fees assessed by other exchanges for proprietary broad-based index options with similarly large notional values, such as S&P 500 Index (“SPX”) options on Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe”).
[
19
]
For these reasons, the Exchange believes that the proposed fee increase, while meaningful in absolute terms, is modest relative to the value of the exposure each contract provides. The Exchange believes the increase will not discourage market participants from transacting in NDX and NDXP options on the Exchange.
Pricing by symbol is a common practice on many U.S. options exchanges as a means to incentivize order flow to be sent to an exchange for execution in particular products. The Exchange notes that market participants are offered different ways to gain exposure to the Nasdaq 100 Index, whether through Nasdaq proprietary products like options overlying NDX, NDXP or XND, or separately through multi-listed options overlying QQQ. Offering such products provides market participants with a variety of choices in selecting the product they desire to utilize in order to gain exposure to the Nasdaq 100 Index. Market participants also may trade competing proprietary broad-based index options on other exchanges, such as SPX and RUT options listed on Cboe.
[
20
]
The Exchange believes that its proposal to increase the Non-Priority Customer NDX and NDXP options fees for regular orders is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the increased fee will be applied uniformly to all Non-Priority Customers. Continuing to assess a lower NDX and NDXP options fees to Priority Customers as compared to Non-Priority Customers is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because Priority Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which attracts Market Makers. An increase in the activity of these market participants in turn facilitates tighter spreads, which may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from other market participants to the benefit of all market participants who may interact with the order flow.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
In terms of intra-market competition, the Exchange will apply the proposed Non-Priority Customer NDX and NDXP options fees uniformly to all Non-Priority Customers. Continuing to assess a lower NDX and NDXP options fees to Priority Customers as compared to Non-Priority Customers does not impose an undue burden on competition because Priority Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which attracts Market Makers. An increase in the activity of these market participants in turn facilitates tighter spreads, which may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from other market participants to the benefit of all market participants who may interact with the order flow.
In terms of inter-market competition, the Exchange notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily favor competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive. In such an environment, the Exchange must continually adjust its fees to remain competitive with other options exchanges. Because competitors are free to modify their own fees in response, and because market participants may readily adjust their order routing practices, the Exchange believes that the degree to which fee changes in this market may impose any burden on competition is extremely limited. As noted above, market participants are offered an opportunity to transact in NDX, NDXP, or XND, or separately execute options overlying QQQ. Offering these products provides market participants with a variety of choices in selecting the product they desire to use to gain exposure to the Nasdaq 100 Index.
In addition to the Exchange, market participants have alternative options exchanges that they may participate on and direct their order flow, which list proprietary products that compete with NDX and NDXP options.
[
21
]
In sum, if the changes proposed herein are unattractive to market participants, it is likely that the Exchange will lose market share as a result. Accordingly, the Exchange does not believe that the proposed changes will impair the ability of members or competing options exchanges to maintain their competitive standing in the financial markets.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act.
[
22
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is: (i) necessary or appropriate in the public interest; (ii) for the protection of investors; or (iii) otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
(
printed page 73337)
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-ISE-2026-57 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-ISE-2026-57. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-ISE-2026-57 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
23
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106859; File No. SR-Phlx-2026-67]
November 9, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 27, 2026, Nasdaq PHLX LLC (“Phlx” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the fees for Nasdaq 100® Index (“NDX”) options and fees for the nonstandard expiration dates (“NDXP”) in the Exchange's Pricing Schedule at Options 7, Section 5.A, and to adopt a new NDX Incentive Program at Options 7, Section 5.B.
While the changes proposed herein are effective upon filing, the Exchange has designated the amendments become operative on November 1, 2026.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​phlx/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to increase NDX and NDXP options pricing for Non-Customers
[
3
]
and adopt a new NDX Incentive Program (“Program”) at Options 7, Section 5.B to offer Market Makers
[
4
]
the opportunity to earn rebates based on market quality metrics in certain NDXP options. Each change is described below.
Transaction Fees
As set forth in Options 7, Section 5.A, the Exchange currently charges all Non-Customer
[
5
]
orders in NDX and NDXP a $0.75 per contract transaction fee. Customer
[
6
]
orders are currently assessed a $0.50 per contract transaction fee in NDX and NDXP. These transaction fees apply to electronic simple and complex executions as well as floor transactions.
The Exchange now proposes to increase the Non-Customer options transaction fees in NDX and NDXP from $0.75 to $1.25 per contract. As a result, Professionals, Lead Market Makers, Market Makers, Broker-Dealers and Firms would each be assessed a transaction fee of $1.25 per contract in NDX and NDXP options, which would continue to apply to electronic simple and complex executions as well as floor transactions. The Exchange is not proposing to amend the Customer transaction fee of $0.50 per contract in NDX and NDXP options, or the transaction fees for other index options in Options 7, Section 5.
The surcharges set forth in the notes to Options 7, Section 5.A would continue to apply, unchanged, in addition to the transaction fees for NDX and NDXP options. Specifically: (i) note
(
printed page 73366)
1 provides that a surcharge of $0.25 per contract is assessed to Non-Customers in NDX and NDXP options; (ii) note 3 provides that a surcharge is assessed to electronic simple Non-Customer orders in NDX and NDXP options that remove liquidity according to a premium schedule, which ranges from $1.00 per contract for premiums of less than $3.00 to $3.00 per contract for premiums greater than or equal to $50.00; (iii) note 5 provides that a surcharge of $0.50 per contract is assessed to all Non-Customer complex executions in NDX and NDXP options; (iv) note 6 provides that a surcharge of $0.25 per contract is assessed to all Customer complex executions in NDX and NDXP options; and (v) note 7 provides that a surcharge of $0.25 per contract is assessed to all market participants for simple and complex executions in NDX and NDXP options with a premium price of $25.00 or greater.
By way of example, under the proposed pricing a Market Maker electronic simple order in NDXP options with a premium of $5.00 that adds liquidity would be assessed $1.50 per contract (the $1.25 transaction fee plus the $0.25 note 1 surcharge), as compared to $1.00 per contract today. If the same order removed liquidity, it would be assessed $3.00 per contract (the $1.25 transaction fee, the $0.25 note 1 surcharge, and the $1.50 note 3 surcharge), as compared to $2.50 per contract today. A Non-Customer complex execution in NDX options with a premium of $30.00 would be assessed $2.25 per contract (the $1.25 transaction fee, the $0.25 note 1 surcharge, the $0.50 note 5 surcharge, and the $0.25 note 7 surcharge), as compared to $1.75 per contract today. By comparison, a Customer complex execution in NDX options with a premium of $30.00 would continue to be assessed $1.00 per contract (the $0.50 transaction fee, the $0.25 note 6 surcharge, and the $0.25 note 7 surcharge).
While the Exchange is increasing the NDX and NDXP Non-Customer Options Transaction Charge, the Exchange believes that market participants will continue to transact NDX and NDXP options on Phlx given the large notional value of NDX. Each options contract has a multiplier of $100, so a single contract represents notional exposure equal to $100 times the index level. For example, at an index level of 20,000, one NDX or NDXP options contract represents approximately $2,000,000 in notional value. At that level, the proposed $1.25 per contract transaction fee represents approximately 0.00625 basis points of notional value, and the proposed $0.50 increase represents approximately 0.0025 basis points. Because the Exchange's transaction fees are assessed per contract regardless of the size of the underlying exposure, the cost of the fee relative to the economic exposure obtained is small. It remains small even after the proposed increase. The Exchange notes that the increase is modest relative to the value of the exposure each NDX and NDXP options contract provides.
NDX Incentive Program
The Exchange proposes to adopt the Program at new Options 7, Section 5.B, titled “Incentive Programs.” The Program is designed to incentivize Market Makers to post tighter, more consistent quotes in short-dated NDXP options, to the benefit of all market participants that trade those options on Phlx.
Program Period.
As proposed in paragraph (a) of proposed Options 7, Section 5.B, the qualification period for the Program would be a calendar month, and the Program would operate month-to-month. Rebates would be paid each calendar month to eligible Market Makers.
Eligible Participants.
As proposed in paragraph (b) of proposed Options 7, Section 5.B, all Market Makers would be eligible for the Program.
Eligible Options and Measurement Windows.
As proposed in paragraph (c)(1), of proposed Options 7, Section 5.B, the Eligible Options would be P.M.-settled Nasdaq-100 Index options (“NDXP”) that (i) expire on the same trading day on which they are traded (“0DTE”) or (ii) expire on the next trading day (“1DTE”). Eligible strike prices would be all strikes divisible by $25, and no moneyness filter would be applied. Whether a particular options series qualifies at a given time would be determined by the bid premium test described below. As proposed in paragraph (c)(2) of proposed Options 7, Section 5.B, the Exchange would measure quoting performance during the following windows (collectively, the “Measurement Windows”), with all times in Central Time: (i) for 0DTE options, 8:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.; and (ii) for 1DTE options, 8:30 a.m. to 3:15 p.m.
Premium Tiers and Maximum Widths.
As proposed in paragraph (d) of proposed Options 7, Section 5.B, the Program would consist of two independently scored Premium Tiers, each with a Bid Premium Range and a Maximum Width. Premium Tier 1 would have a Bid Premium Range of $8.00 up to and including $80.00 and a Maximum Width of $2.00. Premium Tier 2 would have a Bid Premium Range of $0.20 up to but not including $8.00 and a Maximum Width of $1.00. At each Snapshot (described below), the best bid premium submitted by any Market Maker to Phlx through the Specialized Quote Feed (“SQF”)
[
7
]
would determine the applicable Premium Tier and Maximum Width. An options series could qualify for at most one Premium Tier per Snapshot, and an options series whose best Market Maker bid falls outside both Bid Premium Ranges would not be measured at that Snapshot.
Scoring Methodology.
As proposed in paragraph (e)(1) of proposed Options 7, Section 5.B, the Exchange would measure quoting performance at a randomly selected time within each 15-second interval during the applicable Measurement Window (each, a “Snapshot”). As proposed in paragraph (e)(2) of proposed Options 7, Section 5.B, at each Snapshot an options series would constitute a “Qualified Observation” for a given Premium Tier if the best Market Maker bid submitted through SQF in that options series falls within the Bid Premium Range for that Premium Tier. Only the best displayed quote of Market Makers on Phlx would be considered for this purpose, and a Qualified Observation would apply uniformly to all Market Makers for purposes of the Program. As proposed in paragraph (e)(3), for each options series that constitutes a Qualified Observation, a Market Maker would earn a “Performant Quote” tally if the width of its displayed quotation on Phlx (determined from the Market Maker's best displayed bid and best displayed offer) is equal to or less than the applicable Maximum Width for that Premium Tier. A Performant Quote need
(
printed page 73367)
not be the best quote in the market; it would be judged solely against the applicable Maximum Width.
As proposed in paragraph (e)(4) of proposed Options 7, Section 5.B, a Market Maker's Monthly Score for each Premium Tier would be calculated as follows: 70% × (monthly sum of Performant Quotes for 0DTE options ÷ monthly sum of Qualified Observations for 0DTE options) + 30% × (monthly sum of Performant Quotes for 1DTE options ÷ monthly sum of Qualified Observations for 1DTE options). Scores would be calculated to two decimal places (
e.g.,
62.47%).
By way of example, assume that at a particular Snapshot a 0DTE options series has the following quotes: Market Maker 1 (“MM1”) $7.90 × $9.90; Market Maker 2 (“MM2”) $8.00 × $9.00; and Market Maker 3 (“MM3”) $7.80 × $10.00. The best Market Maker bid of $8.00 would qualify the options series for Premium Tier 1, which has a Maximum Width of $2.00. MM1's quote is $2.00 wide, which equals the Maximum Width, so MM1's quote is a Performant Quote even though its bid is below $8.00. MM2's quote is $1.00 wide, which is less than the Maximum Width, so MM2's quote is a Performant Quote. MM3's quote is $2.20 wide, which exceeds the Maximum Width, so MM3's quote is not a Performant Quote. If this were the only Snapshot for the month, there would be one 0DTE Qualified Observation and no 1DTE Qualified Observations, and the Market Makers would be scored as follows: MM1, 70% × (
                    1/1
                    ); MM2, 70% × (
                    1/1
                    ); and MM3, 70% × (
                    0/1
                    ).
Funding and Payouts.
As proposed in paragraph (f) of proposed Options 7, Section 5.B, the Exchange would award rebates each calendar month to the highest-scoring Market Makers in each Premium Tier. In Premium Tier 1, the Market Makers ranked first, second and third would receive monthly rebates of $400,000, $250,000 and $100,000, respectively. In Premium Tier 2, the Market Makers ranked first and second would receive monthly rebates of $150,000 and $50,000, respectively. The Exchange would therefore pay up to $950,000 in total Program rebates in a given month. For each Premium Tier, the Exchange will remove two trading days from each Market Maker's monthly measurement for that Premium Tier, selected in a manner that maximizes the Market Maker's overall Monthly Score for that Premium Tier. The days removed may differ between Premium Tiers. The Removal of Days provision in Options 7, Section 1(b) would also apply to the Program for purposes of excluding days from the Monthly Score;
[
8
]
otherwise, all trading days in the month would count toward the Monthly Score. In the event of identical Monthly Scores, the applicable award(s) would be split evenly among the tied Market Makers.
[
9
]
Reporting.
As proposed in paragraph (g), the Exchange would provide Market Makers with a report of their daily performance via Nasdaq Report HQ. In addition, the Exchange would distribute daily standings to all Market Makers and disclose the Monthly Scores of the top three Premium Tier 1 Market Makers and the top two Premium Tier 2 Market Makers, without identifying the Market Makers.
Voluntary Participation; No Quoting Obligation.
As proposed in paragraph (h), participation in the Program would be entirely voluntary. No Market Maker would be required to participate by quoting in NDXP options, and participation would not create any quoting obligation beyond a Market Maker's existing obligations under the Exchange's rules.
[
10
]
Program Design.
The Exchange has designed the Program to focus on those options series and times in which tight, consistent quoting is most valuable to market participants. The Exchange is limiting the Program to 0DTE and 1DTE NDXP options because these short-dated options account for a significant portion of NDXP trading activity and present heightened quoting risk for Market Makers given their rapid time decay and sensitivity to movements in the underlying index. The Exchange proposes to weight 0DTE performance at 70% and 1DTE performance at 30% because 0DTE options represent the larger share of short-dated NDXP options activity, while 1DTE options remain an important part of the market. The two Premium Tiers, with Maximum Widths of $2.00 for bid premiums of $8.00 up to and including $80.00 and $1.00 for bid premiums of $0.20 up to but not including $8.00, are intended to set width standards that are demanding yet achievable relative to the price of the option, recognizing that higher-priced options are typically quoted with wider absolute spreads. Measuring performance at a randomly selected time within each 15-second interval is designed to reward continuous quality quoting throughout the Measurement Windows, rather than quoting only at predictable times. Fixed, ranked rebates provide Market Makers with a clear, transparent incentive to compete with one another on market quality, while allowing the Exchange to control the total cost of the Program. Finally, distributing daily standings and disclosing the top Monthly Scores without identifying the Market Makers is intended to promote competition among participants by allowing each Market Maker to gauge its performance against the field, while protecting the confidentiality of individual firms' results.
The Exchange is proposing the Non-Customer fee increase and the Program together. While the Exchange is increasing the fees assessed to Non-Customers in NDX and NDXP options, the Program is designed to improve the quality of the NDXP market in which those Non-Customers, as well as Customers, transact. The Exchange believes that tighter, more consistent Market Maker quotes in short-dated NDXP options will improve execution quality for all participants that interact with those quotes, including Non-Customers paying the increased fees.
(
printed page 73368)
Further, Market Makers have the ability to earn rebates through the Program while also enhancing market quality in these options on Phlx.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
11
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
12
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
Transaction Fees
The Exchange believes that its proposal to increase the Non-Customer transaction fees in NDX and NDXP options from $0.75 to $1.25 per contract for electronic simple and complex executions as well as floor transactions is reasonable because Customers will continue to be assessed a lower fee as compared to Non-Customers, and the existing surcharges in NDX and NDXP options will continue to apply unchanged. The Exchange believes that, even with the increase, Non-Customer pricing in NDX and NDXP options will remain competitive and will continue to attract order flow to the Exchange.
The Exchange believes that the proposed Non-Customer transaction fee of $1.25 per contract in NDX and NDXP options is reasonable when considered in relation to the notional value of these products. NDX and NDXP options contracts each have a multiplier of $100, so a single contract represents notional exposure equal to $100 times the index level.
[
13
]
Because the Exchange's transaction fees are assessed per contract regardless of the size of the underlying exposure, the cost of the fee relative to the economic exposure obtained is small. It remains small even after the proposed increase. Viewed another way, a market participant seeking comparable Nasdaq 100 exposure through other products would generally need to trade many more contracts, each of which is subject to its own transaction fees. For example, a market participant seeking exposure equivalent to one NDX contract through options overlying Invesco QQQ Trust (“QQQ”)
[
14
]
would need to trade approximately 41 QQQ options contracts. Those contracts would be subject to per-contract transaction fees of up to $0.22 each on the Exchange for an aggregate cost of approximately $9.02. On a notional-equivalent basis, therefore, the proposed NDX and NDXP options fees remain lower than the cost of obtaining similar exposure through alternative products. The Exchange also notes that the proposed fee is lower in some cases and higher in other cases than fees assessed by other exchanges for proprietary broad-based index options with similarly large notional values, such as S&P 500 Index (“SPX”) options on Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe”).
[
15
]
For these reasons, the Exchange believes that the proposed fee increase, while meaningful in absolute terms, is modest relative to the value of the exposure each contract provides. The Exchange believes the increase will not discourage market participants from transacting in NDX and NDXP options on the Exchange.
At the same time, the Exchange is adopting the Program, which is designed to improve the quality of the NDXP market in which Non-Customers transact. Pricing by symbol is a common practice on many U.S. options exchanges as a means to incentivize order flow to be sent to an exchange for execution in particular products. The Exchange notes that market participants are offered different ways to gain exposure to the Nasdaq 100 Index, whether through the Exchange's proprietary products like options overlying NDX, NDXP or XND, or separately through multi-listed options overlying Invesco QQQ. Offering such products provides market participants with a variety of choices in selecting the product they desire to utilize in order to gain exposure to the Nasdaq 100 Index. Market participants also may trade competing proprietary broad-based index options on other exchanges, such as SPX and Russell 2000 Index (“RUT”) options listed on Cboe.
[
16
]
The Exchange believes that its proposal to increase the Non-Customer transaction fees in NDX and NDXP is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the increased fee will be applied uniformly to all Non-Customers. Continuing to assess a lower fee to Customers as compared to Non-Customers is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which attracts Market Makers. An increase in the activity of these market participants in turn facilitates tighter spreads, which may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from other market participants, to the benefit of all market participants who may interact with the order flow.
The Exchange believes that the Program is reasonable because it is designed to incentivize Market Makers to provide tighter, more consistent quotes in 0DTE and 1DTE NDXP options. Improved market quality benefits all market participants, not only the Market Makers that earn rebates. Tighter quotes reduce the cost of trading for Customers and other participants that interact with Market Maker quotes, more consistent displayed liquidity contributes to price discovery, and higher-quality markets attract additional order flow, which further deepens liquidity on the Exchange.
The Program is also reasonable because rebates are tied to objective, transparent metrics, namely Qualified Observations and Performant Quotes measured at random Snapshots against published Bid Premium Ranges and Maximum Widths, which are applied in the same manner to every Market Maker. The fixed rebate amounts, which total up to $950,000 per month, are reasonable in light of the improvement in market quality the Program is designed to achieve and the effort required of Market Makers to maintain quotes at or within the Maximum Widths throughout the Measurement Windows. Removing two trading days per month in the manner that maximizes each Market Maker's Monthly Score is reasonable because it accommodates occasional technical or market disruptions and applies equally to every participant, and splitting awards evenly among Market Makers with identical Monthly Scores is a fair and objective means of resolving ties.
(
printed page 73369)
The Exchange believes that the Program is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because while participation is entirely voluntary, all Market Maker are eligible for the Program, and all Market Makers would be measured against the same Qualified Observations, Maximum Widths, and scoring formula. Participation does not create any quoting obligation beyond a Market Maker's existing obligations under the Exchange's rules. Limiting the Program to Market Makers is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because, unlike other market participants, Market Makers have quoting obligations under the Exchange's rules
[
17
]
and bear the risks associated with continuously quoting in short-dated options. The Program is designed to reward Market Makers for quoting behavior that only they can provide in this manner, and the resulting improvement in market quality accrues to the benefit of all market participants. Ranking Market Makers and paying fixed rebates to the highest scorers is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because every participant has the same opportunity to achieve a top ranking based on its quoting performance.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
In terms of intra-market competition, the Exchange will apply the proposed Non-Customer transaction fees uniformly to all Non-Customers. Continuing to assess a lower fee to Customers as compared to Non-Customers does not impose an undue burden on competition because Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which attracts market makers. An increase in the activity of these market participants in turn facilitates tighter spreads, which may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from other market participants, to the benefit of all market participants who may interact with the order flow.
The Program does not impose an undue burden on intra-market competition. Participation is voluntary and open to all Market Makers, and all participants are measured against the same objective criteria. Limiting the Program to Market Makers does not impose a burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate because Market Makers are subject to quoting obligations and risks that other market participants do not bear, and the improved market quality the Program is designed to produce benefits all market participants that trade NDXP options on the Exchange. Ranking Market Makers and paying rebates to the highest scorers is intended to promote, rather than burden, competition among Market Makers to provide the best market quality.
In terms of inter-market competition, the Exchange notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily favor competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive, or rebate opportunities available at other venues to be more favorable. In such an environment, the Exchange must continually adjust its fees to remain competitive with other options exchanges. Because competitors are free to modify their own fees in response, and because market participants may readily adjust their order routing practices, the Exchange believes that the degree to which fee changes in this market may impose any burden on competition is extremely limited. As noted above, market participants are offered an opportunity to transact in NDX, NDXP, or XND, or separately execute options overlying QQQ. Offering these products provides market participants with a variety of choices in selecting the product they desire to use to gain exposure to the Nasdaq 100 Index. Likewise, competing options exchanges offer market maker incentive programs, and the Exchange must design the Program to attract and retain Market Maker liquidity in competition with those venues.
In addition to the Exchange, market participants have alternative options exchanges that they may participate on and direct their order flow, which list proprietary products that compete with NDX and NDXP.
[
18
]
In sum, if the changes proposed herein are unattractive to market participants, it is likely that the Exchange will lose market share as a result. Accordingly, the Exchange does not believe that the proposed changes will impair the ability of members or competing options exchanges to maintain their competitive standing in the financial markets.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act.
[
19
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is: (i) necessary or appropriate in the public interest; (ii) for the protection of investors; or (iii) otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-Phlx-2026-67 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-Phlx-2026-67. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is
(
printed page 73370)
obscene or subject to copyright protection.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-Phlx-2026-67 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
20
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

full_text:

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106858; File No. SR-CboeEDGX-2026-075]
(
printed page 73345)
November 9, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 3, 2026, Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “EDGX”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc. (“EDGX” or the “Exchange”) proposes to amend Rule 13.8(b)
[
3
]
to describe the Cboe Aggregated Market (“Cboe One”) Feed by reference to the specific data feeds from which its content is obtained, namely the Multicast Depth feed of the Exchange described in Rule 13.8(a) and the Multicast Depth feeds of its affiliated exchanges and information disseminated by the securities information processors (“SIPs”), and to state that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, which differ in the quotation information each provides, consistent with the manner in which other exchanges describe comparable aggregated market data products. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​equities/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​edgx/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 13.8(b), which currently lists the specific data elements and message types in the Cboe One Feed, to instead identify the sources of the Cboe One Feed: (1) the Multicast Depth feed of the Exchange described in Rule 13.8(a) and the Multicast Depth feeds of BZX, BYX, and EDGA (collectively, the “Multicast Depth Feeds”); and (2) the SIPs. The proposed rule text also states that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, which differ in the quotation information each provides: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders on the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGA, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations for displayed orders on each such exchange at multiple price levels. This approach is consistent with the manner in which other exchange groups describe comparable aggregated market data products by identifying their sources rather than specifying message formats or field-level content, as discussed below.
By way of background, the Cboe One Feed is currently offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, each of which contains information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds and from the SIPs.
[
4
]
The versions differ only in the quotation information each provides. Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations at multiple price levels, currently up to twelve per side per exchange.
[
5
]
Execution information, administrative messages, and consolidated market information are the same in both versions. The current Cboe One Feed includes the following information from the Multicast Depth Feeds: individual last sale information for the Exchange and each of its affiliated exchanges, as well as Symbol Summary, Market Status, Retail Liquidity Identifier, Trading Status, and Trade Break messages. It also includes the following information from the SIPs: consolidated volume, the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, and the current day consolidated high and low price for all listed equity securities. The Cboe One Feed also disseminates the following information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds: the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price. For securities listed on BZX, the Cboe One Opening Price is the BZX Official Opening Price as defined in BZX Rule 11.23(a)(5), and the Cboe One Closing Price is the BZX Official Closing Price as defined in BZX Rule 11.23(a)(3). For securities not listed on BZX, the Cboe One Opening Price is the first last sale eligible trade that occurs on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges after 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time, and the Cboe One Closing Price is the final last sale eligible trade to occur on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges prior to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time. The five price level version of Cboe One Premium is scheduled to be sunset no later than December 31, 2026, and the Exchange announced via Exchange Notice that it will be sunset effective November 2, 2026.
[
6
]
As of that date, Cboe One Premium will be offered only with up to twelve aggregated price levels per side per exchange, which have been available since May 4, 2026.
The Exchange has historically amended Rule 13.8(b) by name each time it added a data element to the Cboe One Feed, even where the new data
(
printed page 73346)
element fell within a type of information the feed already carried. For example, the Exchange filed a proposed rule change to add the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, obtained directly from the SIPs and disseminated after the applicable SIP delay period,
[
7
]
and later filed a separate proposed rule change to add the current day consolidated high and low price, also obtained directly from the SIPs.
[
8
]
Each of these filings added a discrete data element obtained from information disseminated by the SIPs, a source already reflected in the feed. The Exchange now proposes to describe the Cboe One Feed by its sources so that the addition of a data element, or a change to an existing data element, obtained from a source identified in Rule 13.8(b) will not require a separate proposed rule change.
As proposed, Rule 13.8(b) would provide that the Cboe One Feed contains information obtained from two sources: the Multicast Depth Feeds and the SIPs. It would further provide that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, which differ in the quotation information each provides: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders on the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGA, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations for displayed orders on each such exchange at multiple price levels. The proposed rule text would not specify the number of price levels in Cboe One Premium, itemize categories of information, or define “consolidated market information.” Those details describe the current content of the feed, as discussed below. The amended rule would define the Cboe One Feed by the sources from which its content is obtained and by the quotation information each version provides, rather than by a list of individual data elements, message names, prices, or price levels. A recipient would continue to subscribe to either Cboe One Summary or Cboe One Premium.
The proposed rule text deletes from Rule 13.8(b): (i) the itemized list of data elements, including the references to consolidated volume, the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, and the current day consolidated high and low price; (ii) the names of individual messages, including the parenthetical attributing the Retail Liquidity Identifier to BYX; (iii) the Depth of Book subparagraph, including the references to five and twelve price levels and the sunset of the five level feed of Cboe One Premium; and (iv) the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price methodology. In their place, the proposed rule text identifies the Multicast Depth Feeds and the SIPs as the sources of the Cboe One Feed and states that the feed is offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, which differ in the quotation information each provides. The proposed rule change does not change the content of the Cboe One Feed. Each of the deleted items continues to be disseminated through the Cboe One Feed, is described above as part of the current content of the feed, and falls within one of the categories of information described below: quotation information, execution information, administrative messages, and consolidated market information.
Quotation information.
Quotation information is obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds. Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium differ only in the quotation information each includes: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer on the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGA, and Cboe One Premium provides up to twelve aggregated price levels per side per exchange. The five price level version of Cboe One Premium will be sunset effective November 2, 2026, as previously announced.
[
9
]
The number of price levels is an operational parameter of an existing data element rather than a distinct category of information, and any change will be announced in advance via Exchange Notice and reflected in the technical specifications.
[
10
]
Quotation information also includes the Retail Liquidity Identifier of each of BYX and the Exchange, disseminated pursuant to BYX Rule 11.24(e) and Rule 11.21(e), respectively, and obtained from that exchange's Multicast Depth feed.
[
11
]
The Exchange's Retail Liquidity Identifier is currently disseminated through the Cboe One Feed, but Rule 13.8(b) was inadvertently not updated to reflect it. The proposed rule text encompasses both identifiers without naming them, and any new or modified retail liquidity program would be subject to a separate proposed rule change by the applicable exchange.
Execution information.
Execution information is limited to executions on the Exchange and its affiliated exchanges, including last sale, trade break, and symbol summary information and the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price, and is obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds. The proposed rule change does not change the methodology for the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price, which, with the details of each other data element, is set forth in the technical specifications.
[
12
]
Administrative messages.
Administrative messages are status messages related to the other information in the feed, obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds or, for status indicators associated with consolidated market information, from the SIPs.
Consolidated market information.
Consolidated market information is information obtained from the SIPs, together with associated SIP indicators, such as consolidated volume and consolidated price information, and is disseminated consistent with any delay period applicable under the national market system plan(s) governing consolidated equity market data.
[
13
]
The Exchange will file a proposed rule change with the Commission before disseminating through the Cboe One Feed any information not obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds or the SIPs, whether exchange data or otherwise.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange
(
printed page 73347)
and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
14
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
15
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
16
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 11A of the Act
[
17
]
in that it supports (1) fair competition among brokers and dealers, among exchange markets, and between exchange markets and markets other than exchange markets and (2) the availability to brokers, dealers, and investors of information with respect to quotations for and transactions in securities. Furthermore, the proposed rule change is consistent with Rule 603(a) of Regulation NMS,
[
18
]
which provides that any national securities exchange that distributes information with respect to quotations for or transactions in an NMS stock do so on terms that are fair and reasonable and not unreasonably discriminatory.
Describing the Cboe One Feed by source promotes transparency and removes impediments to a free and open market because Rule 13.8(b) will accurately identify the sources of the feed: the Multicast Depth Feeds, each of which is itself described in the rules of the applicable exchange, and the SIPs. The Exchange's Multicast Depth feed is described in EDGX Rule 13.8(a). The details of each data element, including the number of price levels in Cboe One Premium and the methodology for the Cboe One Opening Price and the Cboe One Closing Price, are set forth in the publicly available Cboe One Feed technical specifications, so that market participants can readily determine the content and methodology of each data element disseminated through the feed.
[
19
]
The approach is also consistent with the manner in which other exchange groups describe comparable products. NYSE has described NYSE BQT as consisting of data elements from the existing BBO and Trades feeds of NYSE and its affiliated exchanges, together with consolidated information obtained directly from the SIPs, and as representing “aggregated and consolidated information” of those underlying feeds.
[
20
]
Nasdaq has similarly described Nasdaq Last Sale Plus as, in essence, a product that consolidates information from multiple Nasdaq exchanges and the SIPs.
[
21
]
Most recently, Nasdaq proposed Nasdaq Basic Plus and Nasdaq TotalView Plus, which offer consolidated top of book and depth of book information from Nasdaq and its affiliated exchanges, and which Nasdaq identified as comparable to Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, respectively.
[
22
]
In addition, because the Cboe One Feed is a single product offered jointly by the Exchange and its affiliated exchanges, the Exchange believes that harmonizing the description of the Cboe One Feed across the rules of the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGA, through substantively identical proposed rule changes filed concurrently by each exchange, promotes transparency and consistency and removes impediments to a free and open market by ensuring that market participants and the public can look to the rules of any of the four exchanges and find the same description of the same product.
Finally, the Exchange notes that the Cboe One Feed is distributed and purchased on a voluntary basis, in that neither the Exchange nor market data distributors are required by any rule or regulation to make this data product available. Thus, users of the data product may discontinue use of the product at any time and for any reason.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change will not impose any burden on intramarket competition because the Cboe One Feed will be available to all recipients on the same terms, and the proposal does not amend any fees. The restatement of Rule 13.8(b) by source does not itself change the content of the feed or of either version, and the removal of the specific number of price levels from the rule text does not change the current content of Cboe One Premium, which will continue to be described in the technical specifications and changed only upon advance Exchange Notice. The proposed rule change will not impose any burden on intermarket competition because the Exchange is not the exclusive distributor of the aggregated and consolidated information that comprises the Cboe One Feed. This includes any SIP-based information, which is limited to information that any subscriber to the SIP data feeds could obtain from the SIPs. The Cboe One Feed is an optional product that competes with similar products offered by other exchanges and with the SIPs, and market participants are not required to subscribe to it.
[
23
]
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange has not solicited, and does not intend to solicit, comments on this proposed rule change. The Exchange has not received any unsolicited written comments from Members or other interested parties.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
24
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
25
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the
(
printed page 73348)
proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
26
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
27
]
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
28
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b4(f)(6)(iii),
[
29
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay because the proposed rule change restates the description of the Cboe One Feed in Rule 13.8(b) by source and does not change the content of either version of the Cboe One Feed, or any fee applicable to the Cboe One Feed. Furthermore, the proposed rule change does not raise any new or novel issues, as it is consistent with the manner in which other exchanges describe comparable aggregated market data products, as discussed above. For these reasons, the Commission finds that waiving the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Accordingly, the Commission hereby waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change as operative upon filing.
[
30
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
31
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-CboeEDGX-2026-075 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeEDGX-2026-075. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeEDGX-2026-075 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
32
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGA Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Description of Cboe Aggregated Market Feed (Cboe One) in Rule 13.8
full_text:
