Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106857; File No. SR-CboeEDGA-2026-037]
November 9, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 3, 2026, Cboe EDGA Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “EDGA”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe EDGA Exchange, Inc. (“EDGA” or the “Exchange”) proposes to amend Rule 13.8(b)
[
3
]
to describe the Cboe Aggregated Market (“Cboe One”) Feed by reference to the specific data feeds from which its content is obtained, namely the Multicast Depth feed of the Exchange described in Rule 13.8(a) and the Multicast Depth feeds of its affiliated exchanges and information disseminated by the securities information processors (“SIPs”), and to state that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, which differ in the quotation information each provides, consistent with the manner in
(
printed page 73317)
which other exchanges describe comparable aggregated market data products. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​equities/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​edga/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 13.8(b), which currently lists the specific data elements and message types in the Cboe One Feed, to instead identify the sources of the Cboe One Feed: (1) the Multicast Depth feed of the Exchange described in Rule 13.8(a) and the Multicast Depth feeds of BZX, BYX, and EDGX (collectively, the “Multicast Depth Feeds”); and (2) the SIPs. The proposed rule text also states that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, which differ in the quotation information each provides: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders on the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGX, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations for displayed orders on each such exchange at multiple price levels. This approach is consistent with the manner in which other exchange groups describe comparable aggregated market data products by identifying their sources rather than specifying message formats or field-level content, as discussed below.
By way of background, the Cboe One Feed is currently offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, each of which contains information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds and from the SIPs.
[
4
]
The versions differ only in the quotation information each provides. Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations at multiple price levels, currently up to twelve per side per exchange.
[
5
]
Execution information, administrative messages, and consolidated market information are the same in both versions. The current Cboe One Feed includes the following information from the Multicast Depth Feeds: individual last sale information for the Exchange and each of its affiliated exchanges, as well as Symbol Summary, Market Status, Retail Liquidity Identifier, Trading Status, and Trade Break messages. It also includes the following information from the SIPs: consolidated volume, the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, and the current day consolidated high and low price for all listed equity securities. The Cboe One Feed also disseminates the following information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds: the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price. For securities listed on BZX, the Cboe One Opening Price is the BZX Official Opening Price as defined in BZX Rule 11.23(a)(5), and the Cboe One Closing Price is the BZX Official Closing Price as defined in BZX Rule 11.23(a)(3). For securities not listed on BZX, the Cboe One Opening Price is the first last sale eligible trade that occurs on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges after 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time, and the Cboe One Closing Price is the final last sale eligible trade to occur on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges prior to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time. The five price level version of Cboe One Premium is scheduled to be sunset no later than December 31, 2026, and the Exchange announced via Exchange Notice that it will be sunset effective November 2, 2026.
[
6
]
As of that date, Cboe One Premium will be offered only with up to twelve aggregated price levels per side per exchange, which have been available since May 4, 2026.
The Exchange has historically amended Rule 13.8(b) by name each time it added a data element to the Cboe One Feed, even where the new data element fell within a type of information the feed already carried. For example, the Exchange filed a proposed rule change to add the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, obtained directly from the SIPs and disseminated after the applicable SIP delay period,
[
7
]
and later filed a separate proposed rule change to add the current day consolidated high and low price, also obtained directly from the SIPs.
[
8
]
Each of these filings added a discrete data element obtained from information disseminated by the SIPs, a source already reflected in the feed. The Exchange now proposes to describe the Cboe One Feed by its sources so that the addition of a data element, or a change to an existing data element, obtained from a source identified in Rule 13.8(b) will not require a separate proposed rule change.
As proposed, Rule 13.8(b) would provide that the Cboe One Feed contains information obtained from two sources: the Multicast Depth Feeds and the SIPs. It would further provide that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, which differ in the quotation information each provides: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders on the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGX, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations for displayed orders on each such exchange at multiple price levels. The proposed rule text would not specify the number of price levels in Cboe One Premium, itemize categories of information, or define “consolidated market information.” Those details describe the current content of the feed, as discussed below. The amended rule would define
(
printed page 73318)
the Cboe One Feed by the sources from which its content is obtained and by the quotation information each version provides, rather than by a list of individual data elements, message names, prices, or price levels. A recipient would continue to subscribe to either Cboe One Summary or Cboe One Premium.
The proposed rule text deletes from Rule 13.8(b): (i) the itemized list of data elements, including the references to consolidated volume, the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, and the current day consolidated high and low price; (ii) the names of individual messages, including the parenthetical attributing the Retail Liquidity Identifier to BYX; (iii) the Depth of Book subparagraph, including the references to five and twelve price levels and the sunset of the five level feed of Cboe One Premium; and (iv) the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price methodology. In their place, the proposed rule text identifies the Multicast Depth Feeds and the SIPs as the sources of the Cboe One Feed and states that the feed is offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, which differ in the quotation information each provides. The proposed rule change does not change the content of the Cboe One Feed. Each of the deleted items continues to be disseminated through the Cboe One Feed, is described above as part of the current content of the feed, and falls within one of the categories of information described below: quotation information, execution information, administrative messages, and consolidated market information.
Quotation information.
Quotation information is obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds. Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium differ only in the quotation information each includes: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer on the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGX, and Cboe One Premium provides up to twelve aggregated price levels per side per exchange. The five price level version of Cboe One Premium will be sunset effective November 2, 2026, as previously announced.
[
9
]
The number of price levels is an operational parameter of an existing data element rather than a distinct category of information, and any change will be announced in advance via Exchange Notice and reflected in the technical specifications.
[
10
]
Quotation information also includes the Retail Liquidity Identifier of each of BYX and EDGX, disseminated pursuant to BYX Rule 11.24(e) and EDGX Rule 11.21(e), respectively, and obtained from that exchange's Multicast Depth feed.
[
11
]
The EDGX Retail Liquidity Identifier is currently disseminated through the Cboe One Feed, but Rule 13.8(b) was inadvertently not updated to reflect it. The proposed rule text encompasses both identifiers without naming them, and any new or modified retail liquidity program would be subject to a separate proposed rule change by the applicable exchange.
Execution information.
Execution information is limited to executions on the Exchange and its affiliated exchanges, including last sale, trade break, and symbol summary information and the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price, and is obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds. The proposed rule change does not change the methodology for the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price, which, with the details of each other data element, is set forth in the technical specifications.
[
12
]
Administrative messages.
Administrative messages are status messages related to the other information in the feed, obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds or, for status indicators associated with consolidated market information, from the SIPs.
Consolidated market information.
Consolidated market information is information obtained from the SIPs, together with associated SIP indicators, such as consolidated volume and consolidated price information, and is disseminated consistent with any delay period applicable under the national market system plan(s) governing consolidated equity market data.
[
13
]
The Exchange will file a proposed rule change with the Commission before disseminating through the Cboe One Feed any information not obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds or the SIPs, whether exchange data or otherwise.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
14
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
15
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
16
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 11A of the Act
[
17
]
in that it supports (1) fair competition among brokers and dealers, among exchange markets, and between exchange markets and markets other than exchange markets and (2) the availability to brokers, dealers, and investors of information with respect to quotations for and transactions in securities. Furthermore, the proposed rule change is consistent with Rule 603(a) of Regulation NMS,
[
18
]
which provides that any national securities exchange that distributes information with respect to quotations for or transactions in an NMS stock do so on terms that are fair and reasonable and not unreasonably discriminatory.
Describing the Cboe One Feed by source promotes transparency and removes impediments to a free and open market because Rule 13.8(b) will accurately identify the sources of the feed: the Multicast Depth Feeds, each of which is itself described in the rules of
(
printed page 73319)
the applicable exchange, and the SIPs. The Exchange's Multicast Depth feed is described in EDGA Rule 13.8(a). The details of each data element, including the number of price levels in Cboe One Premium and the methodology for the Cboe One Opening Price and the Cboe One Closing Price, are set forth in the publicly available Cboe One Feed technical specifications, so that market participants can readily determine the content and methodology of each data element disseminated through the feed.
[
19
]
The approach is also consistent with the manner in which other exchange groups describe comparable products. NYSE has described NYSE BQT as consisting of data elements from the existing BBO and Trades feeds of NYSE and its affiliated exchanges, together with consolidated information obtained directly from the SIPs, and as representing “aggregated and consolidated information” of those underlying feeds.
[
20
]
Nasdaq has similarly described Nasdaq Last Sale Plus as, in essence, a product that consolidates information from multiple Nasdaq exchanges and the SIPs.
[
21
]
Most recently, Nasdaq proposed Nasdaq Basic Plus and Nasdaq TotalView Plus, which offer consolidated top of book and depth of book information from Nasdaq and its affiliated exchanges, and which Nasdaq identified as comparable to Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, respectively.
[
22
]
In addition, because the Cboe One Feed is a single product offered jointly by the Exchange and its affiliated exchanges, the Exchange believes that harmonizing the description of the Cboe One Feed across the rules of the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGX, through substantively identical proposed rule changes filed concurrently by each exchange, promotes transparency and consistency and removes impediments to a free and open market by ensuring that market participants and the public can look to the rules of any of the four exchanges and find the same description of the same product.
Finally, the Exchange notes that the Cboe One Feed is distributed and purchased on a voluntary basis, in that neither the Exchange nor market data distributors are required by any rule or regulation to make this data product available. Thus, users of the data product may discontinue use of the product at any time and for any reason.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change will not impose any burden on intramarket competition because the Cboe One Feed will be available to all recipients on the same terms, and the proposal does not amend any fees. The restatement of Rule 13.8(b) by source does not itself change the content of the feed or of either version, and the removal of the specific number of price levels from the rule text does not change the current content of Cboe One Premium, which will continue to be described in the technical specifications and changed only upon advance Exchange Notice. The proposed rule change will not impose any burden on intermarket competition because the Exchange is not the exclusive distributor of the aggregated and consolidated information that comprises the Cboe One Feed. This includes any SIP-based information, which is limited to information that any subscriber to the SIP data feeds could obtain from the SIPs. The Cboe One Feed is an optional product that competes with similar products offered by other exchanges and with the SIPs, and market participants are not required to subscribe to it.
[
23
]
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange has not solicited, and does not intend to solicit, comments on this proposed rule change. The Exchange has not received any unsolicited written comments from Members or other interested parties.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
24
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
25
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
26
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
27
]
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
28
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b4(f)(6)(iii),
[
29
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. For these reasons, the Commission finds that waiving the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Accordingly, the Commission hereby waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change as operative upon filing.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change by the Options Clearing Corporation Relating to the Addition of the Evergreen Provisions to OCC's LRMF

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106856; File No. SR-OCC-2026-011]
November 9, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Exchange Act” or “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 29, 2026, The Options Clearing Corporation (“OCC”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared primarily by OCC. OCC filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)
[
3
]
of the Act and paragraph (f) or Rule 19b-4
[
4
]
thereunder, such that the proposed rule change was immediately effective upon filing with the Commission. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
This proposed rule change would codify the circumstances in which OCC may renew its liquidity facilities without filing an advance notice with the Commission. The proposed change is described in additional detail in Item 3 below.
The proposed changes to OCC's Liquidity Risk Management Framework (“LRMF”) are contained in confidential Exhibit 5 to File No. OCC-2026-011. Material proposed to be added is marked by underlining and material proposed to be deleted is marked with strikethrough text. All terms with initial capitalization not defined herein have the same meaning as set forth in OCC's By-Laws and Rules.
[
5
]
II. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, OCC included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. OCC has prepared summaries, set forth in sections (A), (B), and (C) below, of the most significant aspects of these statements.
(A) Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
OCC maintains certain liquidity facilities to ensure access to needed liquidity in time to satisfy settlement obligations, even in the event of a default by a Clearing Member or another market disruption. These liquidity facilities were each previously the subject of advance notice filings for renewals. At least one advance notice filing relating to each liquidity facility, to which the Commission did not object, sets forth the circumstances under which OCC may renew the facility without filing an additional advance notice (the “Evergreen Provisions”).
[
6
]
These Evergreen Provisions are not presently codified in any OCC rule. OCC now seeks to (1) add these Evergreen Provisions to its LRMF; (2) make non-substantive changes to the language and structure of the Evergreen Provisions and the Liquidity Risk Management Framework for clarity and consistency; and (3) add sub-headings for clarity. OCC believes that codifying the Evergreen Provisions in the LRMF will make them more accessible within OCC and subject to annual review by OCC.
1. Purpose
OCC proposes changes to its LRMF to memorialize the Evergreen Provisions that describe the circumstances in which OCC may renew three liquidity facilities described in detail below without filing an advance notice. Including these Evergreen Provisions will improve the completeness of the LRMF and make it more efficient to track the circumstances in which the facilities may be renewed without an advance notice. Each of the three facilities and the current conditions under which OCC may renew the facility without filing an advance notice are described below.
Revolving Credit Facility
OCC maintains a revolving credit facility for a 364-day term that it may use: (i) to meet obligations arising out of the default or suspension of a Clearing Member or any action taken by OCC to address such a default or suspension; (ii) to reimburse OCC for bankruptcy losses, subject to the conditions set forth in the By-Laws and Rules; (iii) to the extent permitted by the By-Laws and Rules, (a) to obtain funds projected to be required by OCC in anticipation of a potential default by, or suspension of, a Clearing Member; or (b) to address liquidity needs for daily settlement obligations as the result of the failure of any bank, securities or commodities clearing organization, or investment counterparty to perform any obligation to OCC when due (“Revolving Credit Facility”).
[
7
]
The Revolving Credit Facility provides short-term secured borrowings in an aggregate principal amount of $2.5 billion but may be increased to $3.5 billion if OCC so requests and sufficient commitments from lenders are received and accepted. To obtain a loan under the Revolving Credit Facility, OCC would pledge as collateral: (i) U.S. dollars; (ii) securities issued or guaranteed by the U.S. Government or the Government of Canada; (iii) equities included in the S&P 500 Market Index, the NASDAQ exchange, or any United States or Canadian national securities exchange; (iv) Exchange-Traded Funds (“ETFs”); or (v) American Depositary Receipts (“ADRs”). It is renewed annually for a 364-day term.
OCC must submit an advance notice prior to renewing the Revolving Credit Facility if it intends to make changes to the commitment period (which would continue to be 364 calendar days unless changes are necessary to avoid the expiration of the term falling on a weekend or other day that is not a business day).
[
8
]
However, without
(
printed page 73289)
submitting an advance notice, OCC may: (1) increase the commitment amounts so long as the increase (whether in the initial commitment amount, additional commitment amount, or both) is by no more than $500 million in total as compared to the 2025 Bank Syndicate Revolving Credit Facility, which authorized a $2.5 billion initial commitment that could be increased to $3.5 billion if OCC so requests and sufficient commitments from lenders are received and accepted; (2) decrease the commitment amounts by up to $500 million so long as any decrease in the initial commitment amount is replaced by other qualifying liquid resources (as defined in Exchange Act Rule 17ad-22(a)(14)
[
9
]
) of an equal amount;
[
10
]
(3) add new lenders or remove existing lenders so long as all lenders to future renewals are subject to the same credit review as those lenders that were party to its 2020 Bank Syndicate Revolving Credit Facility; (4) change the lead administrative agent and/or the backup administrative agent so long as the new agent in future renewals is subject to the requirements for selecting providers of core services set forth OCC's policies and procedures; (5) change pricing and collateral haircuts,
[
11
]
so long as such terms are consistent with the then-current market practice; and (6) change other terms and conditions of the agreement so long as the changes do not materially affect the nature or level of risk presented to OCC.
Bank Repo Facility
OCC also maintains a master repurchase agreement with a bank counterparty as part of its overall liquidity plan (“Bank Repo Facility”). Pursuant to the Bank Repo Facility, the buyer (
i.e.,
the bank counterparty) agrees to purchase from OCC, from time to time, U.S. Government securities. OCC, as the seller, would transfer these securities to the buyer in exchange for a payment by the buyer to OCC in immediately available funds. The buyer would simultaneously agree to transfer the purchased securities back to OCC at a specified later date or on OCC's demand against the transfer of funds by OCC to the buyer in an amount equal to the amount the buyer paid plus the accrued and unpaid price differential, which is the interest component of the agreement. The buyer provides a funding commitment of up to $1 billion, with the commitment extending for one year (plus or minus one day).
The Bank Repo Facility is renewed annually. OCC would submit another advance notice with respect to such renewal for the same term only if: (i) OCC determines its liquidity needs merit funding levels above the $1 billion, (ii) OCC should seek to change the terms and conditions of the Master Repurchase Agreement (“MRA”) in a manner that materially affects the nature or level of risk presented by OCC,
[
12
]
(iii) OCC should seek to add counterparties or substitute the bank counterparty to the Bank Repo Facility program, or (iv) the bank counterparty has experienced a negative change to its credit profile or a material adverse change since the latest renewal of the MRA.
[
13
]
Non-Bank Liquidity Facility
OCC also maintains a program for accessing additional committed sources of liquidity that do not increase the concentration of OCC's counterparty exposures (“Non-Bank Liquidity Facility”). The Non-Bank Liquidity Facility is comprised of two parts: an MRA and confirmations with one or more institutional investors, which contain certain individualized terms and conditions of transactions executed between OCC, the institutional investors and their agents. The MRA is structured like a typical repurchase arrangement. This facility has no commitment limit, but OCC has established a target across all external liquidity resources of at least $3 billion.
[
14
]
OCC seeks new and renewed commitments of varying term lengths under this facility.
OCC would submit another advance notice with respect to the execution of individual commitments under the Non-Bank Liquidity Facility only if: (i) OCC should seek to execute a commitment at a level that would have the effect of reducing external liquidity below the target of $3 billion; (ii) OCC should seek to change the terms and conditions of the MRA or commitments thereunder in a manner that materially affects the nature or level of risk presented by OCC;
[
15
]
or (iii) OCC should seek to execute a commitment with a counterparty that has experienced a negative change to its credit profile or a material adverse change since OCC last executed a commitment with that counterparty. But OCC may make changes to (i) liquidity providers provided that any new counterparty is subject to a credit review under OCC's Third-Party Risk Management Framework
[
16
]
and (ii) term lengths consistent with those approved by OCC's Board of Directors (“Board”) considering factors including, but not limited to, the initial committed length of the term, market conditions, and OCC's liquidity needs.
[
17
]
Adding the Evergreen Conditions to the LRMF
The current conditions under which OCC may renew its liquidity facilities without filing an advance notice are not codified in any OCC written policy or procedure. Rather, they are documented in the advance notices OCC filed with respect to each liquidity facility, and in the Commission's notices of no objection thereto.
[
18
]
OCC seeks to add
(
printed page 73290)
these Evergreen Provisions to its LRMF, which is designed to effectively identify, measure, monitor, and manage the liquidity risks that arise in or are borne by OCC. A crucial component of the LRMF is OCC's access to a reliable and diverse set of committed liquidity resources, including the three liquidity facilities at issue in this advance notice. Adding the Evergreen Provisions for all three liquidity facilities to the LRMF would improve the overall organization of OCC's liquidity risk processes and would make them more accessible. In addition, adding the Evergreen Provisions to the LRMF would ensure that OCC, its Board, and its Risk Committee review them on an at-least annual basis as part of the review of OCC's risk management policies, procedures and systems. Such review may identify the need to propose changes to the Evergreen Provisions. For example, to the extent that OCC later determines that access to additional liquidity is necessary or appropriate, OCC may determine to increase the maximum amount of commitments it may seek under either the Revolving Credit Facility or Bank Repo Facility. Documenting the Evergreen Provisions in the LRMF would serve as a reminder that such a change would require regulatory filings, thereby improving the clarity of OCC's governance arrangements.
2. Statutory Basis
OCC believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 17A of the Exchange Act
[
19
]
and Rules 17ad-22(e)(3) and (e)(7)
[
20
]
thereunder. In particular, OCC believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act,
[
21
]
which requires, among other things, that the rules of a clearing agency be designed to promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities and, to the extent applicable, derivatives transactions, to assure the safeguarding of securities and funds which are in its custody or control or for which it is responsible, and, in general, protect investors and the public interest. The proposed changes would clarify OCC's ability to renew the liquidity facilities that ensure OCC's liquidity even in turbulent market conditions, allowing OCC to promptly clear and settle transactions, protect market participants' funds, and to protect the markets as a whole. For this reason, the proposed changes to OCC's rules are reasonably designed to promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities and derivatives transactions, to assure the safeguarding of securities and funds which are in its custody or control or for which it is responsible, and, in general, protect investors and the public interest in accordance with Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act.
[
22
]
OCC further believes the proposed rule change is reasonably designed to comply with Rule 17ad-22(e)(3).
[
23
]
In relevant part, this provision requires OCC to establish, implement, maintain, and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to maintain a sound risk management framework for managing, among other things, credit and liquidity risk that include risk management policies, procedures and systems designed to identify, measure, monitor, and manage the range of risks that arise in or are borne by OCC that are subject to review on a specified periodic basis and approved by the Board annually.
[
24
]
The proposed rule change promotes this by codifying the Evergreen Provisions for the three liquidity facilities into a single section of the LRMF. Currently the Evergreen Provisions are contained within three separate Commission notices of no objection to OCC advance notice filings. OCC believes that documenting these provisions into a single section of the LRMF will improve the accessibility of the Evergreen Provisions and make the LRMF a more comprehensive description of the actions OCC takes to manage liquidity risk.
[
25
]
Greater accessibility, in turn, will make the Evergreen Provisions clearer and easier to track. Though moving the Evergreen Provisions to the LRMF does not make them any more binding on OCC than they already are, there are benefits to more efficiently organizing them in one place. For example, including them in the LRMF will subject them to annual review and approval by the Board, which may determine that changes should be made, subject to regulatory review and approval of such changes. Further, the proposed Evergreen Provisions and the LRMF generally is revised for clarity and consistency, with the intent of making it easier to understand and adhere to.
OCC also believes the proposed rule change is reasonably designed to comply with Rule 17ad-22(e)(7).
[
26
]
Rule 17ad-22(e)(7) requires OCC to, in part, establish, implement, maintain, and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to effectively measure, monitor, and manage the liquidity risk that arises in or is borne by the covered clearing agency. OCC's proposed rule change is consistent with Rule 17ad-22(e)(7)
[
27
]
because it facilitates OCC's ability to renew its liquidity facilities that protect OCC and its Clearing Members in the event of a liquidity event caused by a default or other circumstance.
(B) Clearing Agency's Statement on Burden on Competition
Section 17A(b)(3)(I) of the Act
[
28
]
requires that the rules of a clearing agency not impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. OCC does not believe that the proposed rule change would have any impact or impose a burden on competition. The proposed changes to the LRMF do not directly affect Clearing Members, their customers, or the markets that OCC serves. Rather, the changes relate only to OCC's ability to renew liquidity facilities to ensure liquidity in the event of a Clearing Member default or other market disruption, which provides similar benefits to all market participants.
(C) Clearing Agency's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants or Others
Written comments were not and are not intended to be solicited with respect to the proposed change and none have been received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
29
]
and paragraph (f) of Rule
(
printed page 73291)
19b-4
[
30
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The proposal shall not take effect until all regulatory actions required with respect to the proposal are completed.
[
31
]
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules-regulations/​self-regulatory-organization-rulemaking
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-OCC-2026-011 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-OCC-2026-011. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method of submission. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules-regulations/​self-regulatory-organization-rulemaking
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of OCC and on OCC's website at
https://www.theocc.com/​Company-Information/​Documents-and-Archives/​By-Laws-and-Rules
.
Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-OCC-2026-011 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.

32
]

Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106855; File No. SR-NYSENAT-2026-29]
November 9, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1)
[
1
]
of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
2
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
3
]
notice is hereby given that on October 28, 2026, NYSE National, Inc. (“NYSE National” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the Connectivity Fee Schedule regarding colocation services and fees to update the list of included data products. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend the Connectivity Fee Schedule regarding colocation services and fees to update the list of included data products (“Included Data Products”).
Currently, the table of Included Data Products in Colocation Note 4 sets forth the market data feeds that Users
[
4
]
can connect to at no additional cost when they purchase a service that includes access to the LCN or IP network.
[
5
]
The Exchange proposes to update the table of Included Data Products to include NYSE Options Select, a data feed that consists of a subset of data from the OPRA consolidated data feed that has been curated by the Exchange's Affiliate SRO NYSE.
[
6
]
Given the growing number of options series and the increasing popularity of options trading, the OPRA consolidated data feed is
(
printed page 73294)
voluminous and requires market participants to dedicate significant amounts of bandwidth to receive it. The NYSE Options Select data feed would provide market participants the ability to view critical NBBO, trade data, and administrative messages from the OPRA data feed without consuming the full OPRA data set, thereby decreasing bandwidth requirements and costs when compared to the full OPRA data feed. Other exchange groups currently offer similar selections of the OPRA data feed, including the Nasdaq Smart Options
[
7
]
and Cboe Options Lite
[
8
]
data feeds.
To implement the change, the Exchange proposes to update the table of Included Data Products as follows (proposed addition italicized):
NYSE Bonds.
NYSE Options Select.
NYSE Options Select Trades & NBBO
.
NYSE Options Select Trades & NBBO Snapshot
.
NYSE Texas.
NYSE Texas Aggregated Lite.
NYSE Texas BBO.
NYSE Texas Integrated Feed.
NYSE Texas Order Imbalances.
NYSE Texas Trades.
As indicated, the Exchange plans to offer connectivity to two different NYSE Options Select data feeds: NYSE Options Select Trades & NBBO, which includes real-time trades and real-time NBBO updates for all OPRA symbols, and NYSE Options Select Trades & NBBO Snapshot, which includes real-time trades for all OPRA symbols plus an NBBO snapshot at the time of a trade (collectively the “NYSE Options Select data feeds”).
The Exchange does not charge for connectivity to the Included Data Feeds. Accordingly, it would not charge for connectivity to the NYSE Options Select data feeds.
Application and Impact of the Proposed Changes
The proposed rule change would not apply differently to distinct types or sizes of market participants. Rather, it would apply to all Users equally. As is currently the case, the purchase of any colocation service is completely voluntary and the Connectivity Fee Schedule is applied uniformly to all Users.
The proposed change is not otherwise intended to address any other issues relating to colocation services or related fees, and the Exchange is not aware of any problems that Users would have in complying with the proposed change.
Implementation
The proposed rule change will become operational when the NYSE Options Select data feeds are available. The Exchange will announce the date through a customer notice.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
9
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
10
]
in particular, because it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest and because it is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange further believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act,
[
11
]
because it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members and issuers and other persons using its facilities.
The Proposed Rule Change Is Reasonable
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is reasonable and would perfect the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protect investors and the public interest, because adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds would increase the number of Included Data Products available to Users for no additional charge. All Users that voluntarily select to access the LCN or IP network would not be subject to a charge above and beyond the fee paid for the relevant LCN or IP network access. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the proposed change is reasonable because the change would mean that a User would have the option of adding connectivity to additional market data feeds without paying additional charges.
Adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds to the list of Included Data Products would allow a User to connect to the NYSE Options Select data feeds if it wished but would not require it to do so. As currently, a User would be able to determine which Included Data Products, if any, to which it connects, based on what would best serve its needs, tailoring the service to the requirements of its business operations.
By adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds, the proposed change would ensure that the list of Included Data Products was up to date. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is reasonable and would perfect the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protect investors and the public interest, as it would ensure that the description of Included Data Products was complete, ensuring that it is accessible and transparent, and providing market participants with clarity as to what connectivity is included in the purchase of access to the LCN and IP networks.
The Proposed Rule Change Is Equitable and Not Unfairly Discriminatory
The Exchange believes that the proposed change provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members and issuers and other persons using its facilities and does not unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers because adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds would increase the number of Included Data Products available to Users for no additional charge. All Users that voluntarily select to access the LCN or IP network would not be subject to a charge above and beyond the fee paid for the relevant LCN or IP network access. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the proposed change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the change would mean that a User would have the option of adding connectivity to an additional market data feed without paying additional charges.
Further, the Exchange believes that the proposed change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory since, as is true now, the proposed change would not apply differently to distinct types or sizes of Users but would apply to all Users equally. Moreover, adding the proposed additional Included Data Products would allow a User to connect to the NYSE Options Select data feeds if it wished, but would not require it to do so. As now, a User would be able to determine which Included Data Products, if any, to which it connects,
(
printed page 73295)
based on what would best serve its needs, tailoring the service to the requirements of its business operations.
By adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds, the proposed change would ensure that the list of Included Data Products was up to date. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory, as it would ensure that the description of Included Data Products was complete, ensuring that it is accessible and transparent, and providing market participants with clarity as to what connectivity is included in the purchase of access to the LCN and IP networks.
For the reasons above, the proposed changes do not unfairly discriminate between or among market participants that are otherwise capable of satisfying any applicable co-location fees, requirements, terms, and conditions established from time to time by the Exchange.
For these reasons, the Exchange believes that the proposal is consistent with the Act.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange believes that the proposal will not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of Section 6(b)(8) of the Act.
[
12
]
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change does not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds would increase the number of Included Data Products available to Users for no additional charge. All Users that voluntarily select to access the LCN or IP network would not be subject to a charge above and beyond the fee paid for the relevant LCN or IP network access. Accordingly, the change would mean that a User would have the option of adding connectivity to an additional market data feed without paying additional charges.
Adding the proposed additional Included Data Product would allow a User to connect to the NYSE Options Select data feeds if it wished, but would not require it to do so. In this way, the proposed changes would enhance competition by, as now, enabling a User to determine to which Included Data Products, if any, it connects, based on what would best serve its needs, tailoring the service to the requirements of its business operations.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change does not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because, as with the other Included Data Products, it believes it would not be the exclusive method to connect to the NYSE Options Select data feeds. As alternatives to connecting to the NYSE Options Select data feeds as an Included Data Products, a User may connect to the market data feed through another User or through a connection to an Exchange access center outside the data center, third party access center, or third party vendor. In addition, a User may choose instead to connect to a similar product offered by another exchange, such as Nasdaq Smart Options or Cboe Options Lite.
[
13
]
By adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds, the proposed change would ensure that the list of Included Data Products was up to date. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the proposed addition to the description of Included Data Products would make the description more accessible and transparent. In this manner, the proposed change would provide market participants with clarity as to what connectivity is included in the purchase of access to the LCN and IP networks, thereby enhancing competition by ensuring that all Users have access to the same information regarding the Included Data Products.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
14
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
15
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii) thereunder.
[
16
]
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
17
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii),
[
18
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay so that the proposal may become operative immediately upon filing. The Exchange believes that waiver of the 30-day operative delay would allow the Exchange to promptly provide market participants with another choice for obtaining streamlined options data as the Exchange anticipates that the NYSE Options Select data feeds will be ready for launch in fewer than 30 days. The Commission believes that waiver of the operative delay would be consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest because the proposed rule change does not present any novel issues and it would provide investors with an additional option for accessing potentially helpful information that could inform their trading decisions as soon as the feeds are available. Accordingly, the Commission hereby waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change operative upon filing.
[
19
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and
(
printed page 73296)
arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSENAT-2026-29 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSENAT-2026-29. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSENAT-2026-29 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
20
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106854; File No. SR-CboeBYX-2026-041]
November 9, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 3, 2026, Cboe BYX Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “BYX”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe BYX Exchange, Inc. (“BYX” or the “Exchange”) proposes to amend Rule 11.22(i)
[
3
]
to describe the Cboe Aggregated Market (“Cboe One”) Feed by reference to the specific data feeds from which its content is obtained, namely the Multicast Depth feed of the Exchange described in Rule 11.22(c) and the Multicast Depth feeds of its affiliated exchanges and information disseminated by the securities information processors (“SIPs”), and to state that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, which differ in the quotation information each provides, consistent with the manner in which other exchanges describe comparable aggregated market data products. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​equities/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​byx/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.22(i), which currently lists the specific data elements and message types in the Cboe One Feed, to instead identify the sources of the Cboe One Feed: (1) the Multicast Depth feed of the Exchange described in Rule 11.22(c) and the Multicast Depth feeds of BZX, EDGA, and EDGX (collectively, the “Multicast Depth Feeds”); and (2) the SIPs. The proposed rule text also states that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, which differ in the quotation information each provides: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders on the Exchange, BZX, EDGA, and EDGX, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations for displayed orders on each such exchange at multiple price levels. This approach is consistent with the manner in which other exchange groups describe comparable aggregated market data products by identifying their sources rather than specifying message formats or field-level content, as discussed below.
By way of background, the Cboe One Feed is currently offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, each of which contains information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds and from the SIPs.
[
4
]
The versions differ only in the quotation information each provides. Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations at multiple price levels, currently up to twelve per side per exchange.
[
5
]
Execution information, administrative messages, and consolidated market information are the same in both versions. The current Cboe One Feed includes the following information from the Multicast Depth Feeds: individual last sale information for the Exchange and each of its affiliated exchanges, as well as Symbol Summary, Market Status, Retail Liquidity Identifier, Trading Status, and Trade Break messages. It also includes the following information from the SIPs: consolidated volume, the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, and the current day consolidated high and low price for all listed equity securities. The Cboe One Feed also disseminates the following information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds: the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price. For securities listed on BZX, the Cboe One Opening Price is the
(
printed page 73310)
BZX Official Opening Price as defined in BZX Rule 11.23(a)(5), and the Cboe One Closing Price is the BZX Official Closing Price as defined in BZX Rule 11.23(a)(3). For securities not listed on BZX, the Cboe One Opening Price is the first last sale eligible trade that occurs on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges after 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time, and the Cboe One Closing Price is the final last sale eligible trade to occur on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges prior to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time. The five price level version of Cboe One Premium is scheduled to be sunset no later than December 31, 2026, and the Exchange announced via Exchange Notice that it will be sunset effective November 2, 2026.
[
6
]
As of that date, Cboe One Premium will be offered only with up to twelve aggregated price levels per side per exchange, which have been available since May 4, 2026.
The Exchange has historically amended Rule 11.22(i) by name each time it added a data element to the Cboe One Feed, even where the new data element fell within a type of information the feed already carried. For example, the Exchange filed a proposed rule change to add the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, obtained directly from the SIPs and disseminated after the applicable SIP delay period,
[
7
]
and later filed a separate proposed rule change to add the current day consolidated high and low price, also obtained directly from the SIPs.
[
8
]
Each of these filings added a discrete data element obtained from information disseminated by the SIPs, a source already reflected in the feed. The Exchange now proposes to describe the Cboe One Feed by its sources so that the addition of a data element, or a change to an existing data element, obtained from a source identified in Rule 11.22(i) will not require a separate proposed rule change.
As proposed, Rule 11.22(i) would provide that the Cboe One Feed contains information obtained from two sources: the Multicast Depth Feeds and the SIPs. It would further provide that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, which differ in the quotation information each provides: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders on the Exchange, BZX, EDGA, and EDGX, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations for displayed orders on each such exchange at multiple price levels. The proposed rule text would not specify the number of price levels in Cboe One Premium, itemize categories of information, or define “consolidated market information.” Those details describe the current content of the feed, as discussed below. The amended rule would define the Cboe One Feed by the sources from which its content is obtained and by the quotation information each version provides, rather than by a list of individual data elements, message names, prices, or price levels. A recipient would continue to subscribe to either Cboe One Summary or Cboe One Premium.
The proposed rule text deletes from Rule 11.22(i): (i) the itemized list of data elements, including the references to consolidated volume, the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, and the current day consolidated high and low price; (ii) the names of individual messages, including the Retail Liquidity Identifier; (iii) the references to five and twelve price levels and the sunset of the five level feed of Cboe One Premium; and (iv) the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price methodology. In their place, the proposed rule text identifies the Multicast Depth Feeds and the SIPs as the sources of the Cboe One Feed and states that the feed is offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, which differ in the quotation information each provides. The proposed rule change does not change the content of the Cboe One Feed. Each of the deleted items continues to be disseminated through the Cboe One Feed, is described above as part of the current content of the feed, and falls within one of the categories of information described below: quotation information, execution information, administrative messages, and consolidated market information.
Quotation information.
Quotation information is obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds. Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium differ only in the quotation information each includes: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer on the Exchange, BZX, EDGA, and EDGX, and Cboe One Premium provides up to twelve aggregated price levels per side per exchange. The five price level version of Cboe One Premium will be sunset effective November 2, 2026, as previously announced.
[
9
]
The number of price levels is an operational parameter of an existing data element rather than a distinct category of information, and any change will be announced in advance via Exchange Notice and reflected in the technical specifications.
[
10
]
Quotation information also includes the Retail Liquidity Identifier of each of the Exchange and EDGX, disseminated pursuant to Rule 11.24(e) and EDGX Rule 11.21(e), respectively, and obtained from that exchange's Multicast Depth feed.
[
11
]
The EDGX Retail Liquidity Identifier is currently disseminated through the Cboe One Feed, but Rule 11.22(i) does not specifically reflect it. The proposed rule text encompasses both identifiers without naming them, and any new or modified retail liquidity program would be subject to a separate proposed rule change by the applicable exchange.
Execution information.
Execution information is limited to executions on the Exchange and its affiliated exchanges, including last sale, trade break, and symbol summary information and the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price, and is obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds. The proposed rule change does not change the methodology for the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price, which, with the details of each other data element, is set forth in the technical specifications.
[
12
]
Administrative messages.
Administrative messages are status messages related to the other information in the feed, obtained from
(
printed page 73311)
the Multicast Depth Feeds or, for status indicators associated with consolidated market information, from the SIPs.
Consolidated market information.
Consolidated market information is information obtained from the SIPs, together with associated SIP indicators, such as consolidated volume and consolidated price information, and is disseminated consistent with any delay period applicable under the national market system plan(s) governing consolidated equity market data.
[
13
]
The Exchange will file a proposed rule change with the Commission before disseminating through the Cboe One Feed any information not obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds or the SIPs, whether exchange data or otherwise.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
14
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
15
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
16
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 11A of the Act
[
17
]
in that it supports (1) fair competition among brokers and dealers, among exchange markets, and between exchange markets and markets other than exchange markets and (2) the availability to brokers, dealers, and investors of information with respect to quotations for and transactions in securities. Furthermore, the proposed rule change is consistent with Rule 603(a) of Regulation NMS,
[
18
]
which provides that any national securities exchange that distributes information with respect to quotations for or transactions in an NMS stock do so on terms that are fair and reasonable and not unreasonably discriminatory.
Describing the Cboe One Feed by source promotes transparency and removes impediments to a free and open market because Rule 11.22(i) will accurately identify the sources of the feed: the Multicast Depth Feeds, each of which is itself described in the rules of the applicable exchange, and the SIPs. The Exchange's Multicast Depth feed is described in BYX Rule 11.22(c). The details of each data element, including the number of price levels in Cboe One Premium and the methodology for the Cboe One Opening Price and the Cboe One Closing Price, are set forth in the publicly available Cboe One Feed technical specifications, so that market participants can readily determine the content and methodology of each data element disseminated through the feed.
[
19
]
The approach is also consistent with the manner in which other exchange groups describe comparable products. NYSE has described NYSE BQT as consisting of data elements from the existing BBO and Trades feeds of NYSE and its affiliated exchanges, together with consolidated information obtained directly from the SIPs, and as representing “aggregated and consolidated information” of those underlying feeds.
[
20
]
Nasdaq has similarly described Nasdaq Last Sale Plus as, in essence, a product that consolidates information from multiple Nasdaq exchanges and the SIPs.
[
21
]
Most recently, Nasdaq proposed Nasdaq Basic Plus and Nasdaq TotalView Plus, which offer consolidated top of book and depth of book information from Nasdaq and its affiliated exchanges, and which Nasdaq identified as comparable to Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, respectively.
[
22
]
In addition, because the Cboe One Feed is a single product offered jointly by the Exchange and its affiliated exchanges, the Exchange believes that harmonizing the description of the Cboe One Feed across the rules of the Exchange, BZX, EDGA, and EDGX, through substantively identical proposed rule changes filed concurrently by each exchange, promotes transparency and consistency and removes impediments to a free and open market by ensuring that market participants and the public can look to the rules of any of the four exchanges and find the same description of the same product.
Finally, the Exchange notes that the Cboe One Feed is distributed and purchased on a voluntary basis, in that neither the Exchange nor market data distributors are required by any rule or regulation to make this data product available. Thus, users of the data product may discontinue use of the product at any time and for any reason.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change will not impose any burden on intramarket competition because the Cboe One Feed will be available to all recipients on the same terms, and the proposal does not amend any fees. The restatement of Rule 11.22(i) by source does not itself change the content of the feed or of either version, and the removal of the specific number of price levels from the rule text does not change the current content of Cboe One Premium, which will continue to be described in the technical specifications and changed only upon advance Exchange Notice. The proposed rule change will not impose any burden on intermarket competition because the Exchange is not the exclusive distributor of the aggregated and consolidated information that comprises the Cboe One Feed. This includes any SIP-based information, which is limited to information that any subscriber to the SIP data feeds could obtain from the SIPs. The Cboe One Feed is an optional product that competes with similar
(
printed page 73312)
products offered by other exchanges and with the SIPs, and market participants are not required to subscribe to it.
[
23
]
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange has not solicited, and does not intend to solicit, comments on this proposed rule change. The Exchange has not received any unsolicited written comments from Members or other interested parties.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
24
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
25
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
26
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
27
]
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
28
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b4(f)(6)(iii),
[
29
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay because the proposed rule change restates the description of the Cboe One Feed in Rule 11.22(j) by source and does not change the content of either version of the Cboe One Feed, or any fee applicable to the Cboe One Feed. Furthermore, the proposed rule change does not raise any new or novel issues, as it is consistent with the manner in which other exchanges describe comparable aggregated market data products, as discussed above. For these reasons, the Commission finds that waiving the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Accordingly, the Commission hereby waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change as operative upon filing.
[
30
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
31
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-CboeBYX-2026-041 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeBYX-2026-041. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeBYX-2026-041 and should be submitted on or before December 4, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
32
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Arca, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Connectivity Fee Schedule
full_text:
